#2177. I tifosi della Lazio chiedono il rinnovo di Danilo Cataldi

Sotto l’ultimo post ufficiale della Lazio, i tifosi chiedono al club di prolungare il contratto del centrocampista.

Sotto l’ultimo post pubblicato dal profilo ufficiale della Lazio, dove si ufficializzava il rinnovo di Floriani Mussolininfino al 2031, molti tifosi biancocelesti hanno rivolto la stessa richiesta alla società. Vogliono che Danilo Cataldi resti e che il club gli rinnovi il contratto.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

«Rinnovate #Cataldi» e «Ora Danilo» sono due dei messaggi comparsi nei commenti. Due formule diverse per esprimere lo stesso desiderio, quello di continuare a vedere il centrocampista con la maglia biancoceleste.

I messaggi raccontano l’affetto per un giocatore diventato un punto di riferimento dentro e fuori dal campo. La richiesta dei tifosi è rivolta alla società, a cui spetta la decisione sul futuro del centrocampista.

#2176. Ranocchia: "Questo l'unico problema dell'Inter. Partitone col Como. Mercato? Ecco chi comprerei"

Ranocchia: "Questo l'unico problema dell'Inter. Partitone col Como. Mercato? Ecco chi comprerei"

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

Intervenuto ai microfoni di Sport Mediaset, Andrea Ranocchia ha analizzato il momento che sta attraversando l'Inter. Dopo la sconfitta nel derby, i nerazzurri hanno saputo rialzarsi battendo Feyenoord e Como con prestazioni convincenti. "Bilancio ottimo, è una squadra forte, in salute, che ha un organico molto ampio. È una squadra che può correre per tutti e tre gli obiettivi. Si è rifnorzata ulteriormente quest'anno, squadra molto competitiva in Italia e in Europa".

"Col Como ha fatto un partitone, è partita aggressiva, ripartita, non ha fatto giocare il Como che è una delle squadre che gioca meglio in Italia e in Europa a livello di calcio. È una squadra che sa di essere forte, vince da anni, ha un gruppo molto solido. L'unico problema dell'Inter può essere l'Inter, quando sai di essere forte, può capitare che abbassi un po' l'attenzione, magari rischi di andare sotto, però può capitare ma è una cosa che si può mettere a posto in un secondo".

"Col Como si è vista una risposta molto forte, probabilmente il fatto che si sono parlati e hanno capito che per vincere devono affrontare in maniera giusta tutta la partita. Comprerei un giocatore che ti può saltare l'uomo sulla fascia, che ti può creare superiorità. Un giocatore che ti riesce a saltare l'uomo quando affronti squadre molto chiuse".

#2174. Lazio-Roma, biglietti: abbonamento o fidelity card per ogni intestatario

Per ciascun biglietto va inserito il numero della card associata all’intestatario; il limite è di quattro acquisti per account.

La S.S. Lazio comunica due finestre di vendita riservata per i biglietti di Lazio-Roma. Secondo quanto riportato da S.S. Lazio, Dalle 10:00 dell’11 novembre alle 23:59 del 15 novembre l’acquisto è riservato agli abbonati alla stagione 2025/2026. Dalle 16:00 del 16 novembre alle 23:59 del 25 novembre potranno acquistare i possessori delle fidelity card Millenovecento ed Eagle Card.

Nella prima finestra, con un account si possono acquistare fino a quattro biglietti. Per ogni intestatario va inserito il numero della card associata al relativo abbonamento: non è sufficiente che sia abbonato soltanto chi effettua l’acquisto. Le indicazioni della Lazio precisano infatti che tutti gli intestatari dei biglietti devono essere abbonati alla stagione passata.

L’elenco delle comunicazioni sui tagliandi comprende anche un avviso dedicato alla vendita riservata agli abbonati del Settore Sud e Aquilotti per Lazio-Roma. Compare inoltre un avviso sulla seconda fase di vendita per gli abbonati alla stagione 2025/26 e per i possessori di fidelity card.

La finestra successiva è destinata ai titolari di Millenovecento ed Eagle Card. Anche in questa fase il limite è di quattro biglietti per account: per ciascun intestatario occorre indicare il numero della card associata. Tutte le persone a cui sono intestati i biglietti devono quindi essere titolari di una fidelity card.

Fra gli avvisi relativi a Lazio-Roma figurano anche quello sulla terza fase, dedicata alla vendita libera dei tagliandi, e il pack di tre partite che comprende Lecce, Atalanta e Roma.

#2173. Is Jobe Bellingham England's next big thing who shares his older brother's 'X-Factor' - or a 'problem child' whose dad blows up at his bosses? Inside the rise of the 21-year-old after first call-up

Published: 09:16 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 16:31 EST, 6 November 2026

For years, Jobe Bellingham has been in the shadows of his older brother Jude.

Now, for the first time since they were children, the duo are poised to perform on the same stage. Only this time it won't be under the lampposts of Stourbridge, but the floodlights at Wembley.

Jobe, 21, has been called up to England's senior squad for the first time and is often described in similar terms to his elder sibling: relentlessly ambitious, focused, and a quick learner who is wise beyond his years.

'You have to have an X-Factor and Jobe does,' said Regis Le Bris, his old manager at Sunderland.

That X-Factor appears to run in the Bellingham blood. Earlier this week Jude was unveiled as the new underwear heart-throb for Calvin Klein, channelling his inner David Beckham in a smouldering photoshoot. No pressure, Jobe.

Their main difference on the pitch is that Jobe, while versatile, tends to occupy a deeper-lying role in midfield – and that actually increases the chances of Thomas Tuchel fielding them together. There is every chance that, against Croatia or Spain next week, we will see just the fourth pair of brothers to feature for England since the Second World War.

Jude and Jobe Bellingham's dream of playing for England together may finally come true

The duo grew up playing together and both joined the Birmingham City academy (Instagram: judebellingham)

The duo visited the Spanish Grand Prix in September with matching shirts and haircuts

They share a close relationship and in September were VIP guests of McLaren for the Spanish Grand Prix, posing for photographs in matching blue shirts and identical haircuts, a mischievous double act.

If you were a few pints deep in the Formula One hospitality area, you'd be forgiven for thinking they were the same bloke – especially when their footballing trajectories are so similar.

Jobe began his career at Birmingham City, like Jude, before moving to Sunderland and now Borussia Dortmund, where his brother also played. Jobe, who is two years younger than his superstar brother, is now in his second full season with the Westphalia giants.

He has previously admitted his trepidation at following in Jude's footsteps, once telling the German club's in-house media channel: 'I was biased against joining Borussia Dortmund for a very long time.

'I had anxieties, fears, and you want to be your own man. But I don't think I should let those stop me from making the right decision.'

The comparisons are inevitable, though, when you share the same name and your potential also happens to be through the ceiling. It is a theme Jobe will simply have to contend with wherever he roams.

In Dortmund's 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich on Saturday, the resemblance was striking as he delivered a standout performance – even having the ball in the back of the net, though his goal was ruled out for a Carney Chukwuemeka foul.

At one stage, Bellingham backheeled the ball over Aleksandar Pavlovic, won the ball back off Dayot Upamecano, drifted past Pavlovic with a skill that left him on one knee, and drove about 30 yards towards goal before firing a shot just over the bar.

They would be just the fourth pair of brother to play for England since the Second World War

Jude and Jobe are pictured together at a Louis Vuitton Paris Fashion Week show in 2023

In that ten-second flash, he displayed the sort of tenacity, ingenuity, and swagger which we have come to associate with Jude.

While not as brazen on the surface as Jude, Jobe perhaps gets some of his confidence from their father Mark.

The brothers were introduced to football by their dad, a retired police sergeant who also scored 700 goals in non-league.

Raising his sons in the West Midlands alongside their mother Denise, Mark gave them tips on how to improve and how to deal with the pressures of football. Jude even describes his father as his first footballing hero.

The crackerjack duo have always competed to see who can be the most precocious. Jude became Birmingham City's youngest-ever player when he debuted for them in 2019. When Jobe made his bow for them in 2022, he did so just 69 days older.

He earned his move to Sunderland after just 26 games and was a hit on Wearside. In his second campaign, he won the Championship Young Player of the Season award and helped them to promotion via the play-offs.

Manager Le Bris was breathless in his praise. 'There are many [qualities], there is a long list,' he said. 'Probably his ambition is one of the first ideas I have when I think about Jobe.

'He is very ambitious but this ambition is not naive. It is connected with what he is doing every day in training and every game on the pitch.

Jude pictured with his brother Jobe, father Mark, and mother Denise upon signing for Borussia Dortmund in 2020

'He has many good qualities as a footballer. He is very powerful and he understands the game very well. He is really interested in the game and, because of that, he is able to improve with experiences. He can learn very quickly.

'He is older than his age. He has more maturity. He is like an exception in the sport. It is not easy to play at the level he is doing so at his age, but he is doing so well.'

In the summer of 2025, Dortmund got on the blower. They were willing to pay £31million – more than they had for Jude – and put him straight in the squad for the Club World Cup. Dortmund's UK scout is Daniel Dodds, the brother of Mike, who had worked with Jobe in Birmingham's academy and at Sunderland.

'I think he can go to the very top,' Mike told the Northern Echo in 2023. 'Both brothers have a very similar mindset in terms of their relentlessness in their pursuit of where they want to get to.'

Despite the extravagant projections, Jobe's time in Germany's industrial belt has not been entirely smooth. Often he has been left to simmer on the bench, unable to nail down a regular starting spot.

In his first Klassiker experience, he came on only to lose the ball and have Michael Olise's shot deflect in off him. One report described him as a man who looked 'completely stripped of confidence'.

On the opening day of last season against St Pauli, he was hauled off at the break, leading to his father going ballistic and allegedly confronting sporting director Sebastian Kehl. That put Jobe in an awkward spot. He was also sent off for a professional foul against Freiburg.

Amid his struggles to adapt to the Bundesliga, he has copped criticism off the ferocious pundit Dietmar Hamann, who blasted him as a 'problem child' in a column for Sky Sport. 'Young, expensive and, so far, not even half as good as Jude Bellingham,' seethed the former Liverpool midfielder.

Jobe has become a more regular starter since the turn of the year and, in any case, has always been highly thought of in English football circles.

Jobe helped Sunderland to promotion from the Championship - manager Regis Le Bris said he had the 'X-factor'

Lee Carsley made Jobe his captain for the Under-21s and waxed lyrical about him: 'I think he will be an all-round box-to-box player. He can be creative, score goals. I still feel he can score more goals.

'His shooting is excellent, especially in training. He can link and receive in tight areas.'

Carsley added: 'He’s a good example to the rest of the group, the way he conducts himself on and off the pitch, the way he prepares, the influence he has on the rest of the team.

'He’s a player who can grow into that role. We just assume that players understand leadership and how that works. It will be good to add another string to his bow and keep improving his game.'

After his U21s debut against Spain in Cadiz, he was ambushed by people who wanted signatures... on their Real Madrid shirts. It was opportune and distasteful, but reflected the bigger picture: the name Bellingham is associated with Jude.

Now Jobe's moment has come. Tuchel picked him partly because of Carsley jabbering on with praise in his ear over recent months. The noise around him has become unavoidable and, with Alex Scott injured and Myles Lewis-Skelly suspended for the first game, the Three Lions are light in midfield.

'To play with my brother for England that would be the biggest dream of my life. Nothing would even get close to that,' Jude said in 2024. That may soon be a reality.

#2172. Pisa, Sapola brilla allo Spezia: Bologna e Frosinone sulle tracce del difensore

Il rendimento di Motiejus Sapola ha attirato rapidamente l'attenzione anche fuori dalla Liguria. Il difensore lituano classe 2006, di proprietà del Pisa e arrivato allo Spezia in prestito durante l'estate, si è imposto fin da subito come uno dei punti fermi della squadra, contribuendo alla partenza positiva dei liguri, attualmente in vetta al Girone B di Serie C.

Le prestazioni del giovane centrale non sono passate inosservate e hanno attirato l'interesse di altri club. In particolare, Bologna e Frosinone hanno inserito il suo nome nella lista dei giocatori da seguire, interessandosi alla sua crescita.

Il futuro di Sapola passa però dagli accordi già definiti tra Pisa e Spezia. Due clausole che, secondo quanto riportato da La Nazione, verranno esercitate da entrambe le società. Sarà dunque il Pisa ad avere l'ultima parola sul futuro del difensore, nonostante l'interesse delle altre pretendenti.

#2171. West Ham need to sign Newcastle United man in January to fix problem position: Opinion

West Ham’s new boss Scott Parker will be looking to put his own stamp on his newly inherited squad with some reinforcements this winter. WHUFC have slipped out of the Championship play-offs after 15 fixtures as they eye an immediate promotion back to the Premier League.

The Hammers need to bring in a new goalkeeper amid Mads Hermansen‘s struggles. They should target a move for Newcastle United stopper Nick Pope, who is facing an uncertain long-term future in the North East and is likely to move on for a new challenge soon.

Pope, 34, is a vastly experienced player and would fit the bill for Parker’s side if they managed to lure him down to the London Stadium. He has been on the books of his current club since joining them back in the summer of 2022 and he has since made 131 appearances in all competitions, 36 of which came last season.

However, the veteran, who has made 10 caps for England in the past, has slipped down the pecking order at Newcastle United over recent times behind Lukas Hornicek. Therefore, he is likely to be available.

Pope would be a safe pair of hands between the sticks for West Ham and has played just under 450 games in his career to date. He is someone who WHUFC could trust and he has top flight pedigree.

He is out of contract at the end of this campaign. Newcastle United risk losing him for free if they don’t sell him in the next transfer window meaning the Hammers could try and get him for a cut-price fee.

The Cambridgeshire-born man played for Charlton Athletic from 2011 to 2016 before Burnley came calling. He then went on to make 155 outings for the Clarets during his time at Turf Moor and was their first choice.

Pope hasn’t played in the second tier for 10 years now but may have to drop down a division now to get first-team football. West Ham would be the perfect destination for him and he would be guaranteed regular game time there under Parker.

West Ham have conceded too many goals this term and a new ‘keeper needs to be a priority. Hermansen has become a bit of a liability for WHUFC, whilst Alphonse Areola is out of favour.

If the price is right, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see Newcastle United allow Pope to head out the exit door. A change of scene would do him good and a switch to the Hammers would suit all parties involved. He was linked with Hull City and Ipswich Town earlier this year.

Parker‘s men lost 2-1 away at Blackburn Rovers last time out. They are back in action next weekend at home to Preston North End.

#2169. Bucchioni: “Napoli? Allegri è un allenatore in difficoltà, la squadra è usurata”

Enzo Bucchioni, giornalista, ha parlato del Napoli negli studi di Sportitalia: “Va analizzata sotto l’aspetto psicologico. Allegri è un allenatore in difficoltà, si vede anche dalla postura del corpo. Lui lo sa benissimo che ha sulle spalle l’esonero dalla Juventus, il brutale esonero dal Milan, che non ha ancora digerito e che ha dimostrato di avere ancora dentro di sè nello sfogo dopo la Roma. Ha tirato in ballo, guarda caso, il Milan, perché è qualcosa che si porta ancora dentro. Va nello spogliatoio, gli succede un’altra cosa, viene contestato e cosa dice a se stesso? «Sono ancora il più forte». Quasi come se volesse sentirselo dire da fuori, ma se lo dice da solo per caricarsi. un posto dopo quell’esonero che comunque gli brucia ancora sulla pelle. Questa è la prima cosa. Dal punto di vista calcistico, torno a quello che diceva Credendino, perché tutto è nato da lì. Quando Antonio Conte mi dice: «Io non parteciperò a un funerale, non accompagno il morto», quella frase andava analizzata, non come una battuta sul fatto che Conte frequenta un ristorante da cento euro, come fece… Lui ha voluto dire una cosa ben precisa: questa squadra è usurata. E’ usurata da due Scudetti, molti giocatori sono gli stessi, è usurata dal punto di vista fisico, è vecchia e andava cambiata profondamente”.

#2167. Mandas, il bomber della Lazio è in porta: almeno dieci punti con le parate

Contro il Napoli il portiere greco è stato premiato come migliore in campo dopo gli interventi su Hojlund e De Bruyne.

Almeno dieci dei 29 punti della Lazio portano la firma delle parate di Christos Mandas. Anche contro il Napoli il portiere greco è stato decisivo: dal Maradona è tornato con il premio di migliore in campo. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, È il rendimento tra i pali a fare di lui, nell’immagine proposta da Il Messaggero, una sorta di bomber biancoceleste.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Gattuso ha puntato su Mandas e, come ha confermato lo stesso allenatore, ha dato il via libera alla cessione di Ivan Provedel. La scelta serviva ad alleggerire la pressione sul greco e a permettergli di sentirsi il titolare per l’intera stagione, dopo sei mesi al Bournemouth senza giocare. Edoardo Motta, messosi in luce l’anno scorso, è invece pronto a tornare nel ruolo di secondo portiere: per lui c’è ancora tempo per crescere.

Il greco conta quattro partite senza subire gol, come Vicario della Juventus e Caprile del Cagliari. La difesa della Lazio è la meno battuta del campionato, con nove reti incassate, e Mandas ha una percentuale di parate dell’81,3%, superiore a quella di Svilar.

Secondo i dati riportati, ha evitato 5,9 gol: soltanto Palmisani del Frosinone ha fatto meglio. La sua media è di 0,8 reti subite ogni 90 minuti. In quest’ultima graduatoria risulta terzo dietro Svilar e Butez, che però hanno disputato meno partite.

Gli interventi sono 39 su 49 tiri subiti. Nei gol incassati, il quotidiano non gli attribuisce responsabilità. Il suo rendimento nelle singole gare non è mai sceso sotto la sufficienza, a conferma della continuità con cui ha accompagnato il percorso biancoceleste.

Mandas ha affrontato un rigore in questa stagione e lo ha parato a Yeaboah del Venezia. Turati del Sassuolo, proprio contro la Lazio, ne ha respinti due. Il dato si aggiunge alle parate con cui il greco ha protetto la difesa meno battuta della Serie A.

Al Maradona si è distinto per il colpo di reattività su Hojlund, arrivato alla fine del primo tempo e finito sulle prime pagine di diversi giornali. Davanti a De Bruyne è rimasto in piedi: Belahyane ha poi sventato l’ultima seria minaccia della partita. Un intervento individuale seguito dal lavoro di squadra richiesto da Gattuso e recepito dai biancocelesti.

Mandas ha dato il proprio contributo nelle partite della Lazio, con un’eccezione nella visibilità del suo lavoro: contro il Sassuolo i biancocelesti hanno dilagato e del portiere si è parlato poco. Il bilancio resta quello di almeno una decina di punti legati alle sue prestazioni, sui 29 raccolti dalla squadra, a undici punti dalla quota salvezza richiamata dal quotidiano.

#2166. 34-year-old must be added to Millwall’s 25-man squad after initial omission: Opinion

Millwall will be thankful to head into the international break with not too much damage done to their play-off chances. The Lions have seven fewer points than they did this time last year. Their latest performances do not indicate a side that will challenge for promotion once again.

Aside from injuries, a tactical problem Alex Neil is facing is in midfield. With a young duo of Jenson Metcalfe and Derek Mazou-Sacko, the South London outfit are being exploited in the middle of the pitch and experience is needed desperately

Casper De Norre is currently sidelined, and Millwall don’t have many senior figures in that position. With Massimo Luongo failing to make the Lions’ 25-man squad, his absence is hurting the Lions in the opening half of the season.

Millwall signed Luongo in the 2025 summer transfer window after his exit from Ipswich Town. The Australian was initially recruited to be a secondary option for the Lions. However, he quickly became a regular in the starting XI until an ACL injury against QPR ruled him out for the rest of the term.

His experience was invaluable to Neil’s side in the opening 10 games of the 2025/26 campaign. When the 34-year-old was involved, the South London outfit lost just twice. They could use his Championship expertise during their horrid run of form.

Metcalfe and Mazou-Sacko have a combined 44 Championship appearances, which is a fraction of the 245 Luongo has. While the duo haven’t been poor on a personal level, their positional awareness can be lacking, which is why Millwall have been caught out four times on the counter-attack.

In just nine second-tier games last term, Luongo made 10 interceptions and conceded just six goals whilst he was on the pitch. The Lions need to improve their defensive record, and the Australian would certainly help.

Luongo has featured several times for Millwall’s development squad to rebuild his fitness. However, there will undoubtedly be questions about whether he will be the same player after his injury. Regardless, given the Lions’ frustrations in midfield, Neil should want the 34-year-old in his squad for the rest of the season.

Obviously, the Australian can’t play until January, when the transfer window opens, with the next squad able to be submitted at the beginning of February. However, the Lions will improve when he is available for selection.

Luongo was dispossessed just five times last campaign and won 52% of his duels. His 47 recoveries in nine games were crucial to Millwall’s early fortunes last year. His involvement this term could help Neil’s side become a side that is contending again.

#2165. He had the world at his feet when he signed for Real Madrid at 13, mixing with Zidane and Ronaldo. Now Jack Harper plays in Italy's Serie D... but he's not giving up on his Scotland dream

Published: 13:06 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 17:10 EST, 6 November 2026

Whatever the Italian word is for ‘steamie’, the steady migration of Scottish players to Serie A has been the talk of it.

The exploits of Scott McTominay and Billy Gilmour at Napoli have been comprehensively documented. Che Adams is thriving at Torino where he now shares a dressing room with Nathan Patterson. You can count Kieron Bowie, Josh Doig, Lennon Miller and Liam Henderson among the diaspora, too.

However, another Scot’s switch to Italy has largely flown under the radar. Back in July, Jack Harper, the former Real Madrid wonderkid and presumed saviour of Scottish football, signed a one-year deal with ASD Nuova Igea Virtus.

Currently playing in Serie D, the fourth tier of the Italian national league pyramid, the Sicilian part-timers were founded in 1946 and subsequently re-founded in 1964, 2011 and again in 2019. Which is to say they’ve had a complicated existence.

Harper can surely relate. Now 30, the Malaga-born frontman was 13 when he first made headlines, signing with Real Madrid after impressing in a youth football tournament. He spent almost six years with Los Blancos, learning his trade in its exalted ‘La Fabrica’ academy under the watchful eye of top coaches, Fernando Morientes and Zinedine Zidane amongst them.

If he wasn’t bumping into Cristiano Ronaldo in the swimming pool, he was having a blether with Gareth Bale or studying Luka Modric. All the while, he was quietly developing, establishing himself as one of the top scorers in multiple age groups within the academy.

Jack Harper now plies his trade in Italy's Serie D with Sicilian club ASD Nuova Igea Virtus

Soon after his 18th birthday, and with Real’s youth structure under review, he decided to swap Madrid for Brighton, signing a two-year deal with the then English Championship side. He couldn’t have known it at the time, but Harper’s move to the Amex Stadium was the start of a frustratingly nomadic decade.

A catalogue of injuries and bad luck kick-started a footballing odyssey that has taken in spells at Malaga, Getafe, Alcorcón, Cartagena and Villarreal, as well as Racing Santander, Hércules, Marbella, Linense and, more recently, Spanish fourth-division outfit Linares.

Harper joined the latter ahead of the 2025-26 season and made an encouraging start, scoring four goals in his first nine appearances before, once again, injury struck. He spent almost four months on the sidelines and, when the campaign ended, he found himself a free agent once more.

‘At that point, I decided to forget all about it until after the World Cup,’ he tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘I said to my family I didn’t want to think about it. I needed to just disconnect.’

He and his brother Ryan travelled to Miami to take in Scotland’s final group match against Brazil and, standing shoulder to shoulder with the Tartan Army in the stands of the Hard Rock Stadium, he allowed himself to wonder what might have been.

‘It was definitely in the back of my mind that I could have been on the pitch because that’s the type of person I am,’ says Harper. ‘I know that if the road was a bit straighter and I’d had just a little more luck, then absolutely, I could have been there representing my country.

Harper had the world at his feet when he signed for Real Madrid at the tender age of 13

‘Years ago, I was knocking on the door when I was playing in Spain. I was called up to the 30-man squad several times but then the injuries started to hit and the door kind of closed. So yeah, of course I was at the stadium thinking I should have been playing. I know the level of football I’m capable of. I just never got a chance to show it.

‘But being there was a cool experience. The atmosphere was unbelievable and to see us taking on a Brazil side dressed in the yellow jerseys with those five stars on them, it was incredible. The World Cup’s the pinnacle of football. I was just glad to be part of it somehow.’

After that party in the US, Harper returned to Spain to discover he was a man in demand.

‘I had a few interesting offers on the table,’ he smiles. ‘I spoke with my partner and we agreed that, whilst our preference was to stay in Spain, it might be wise for us to consider all options. Last season was really hard and so we thought that maybe a change of scenery would do us all good.

‘Next thing I knew, I had an offer from a team in Iraq. There was an opportunity with a team in Thailand, too. That was very, very close to being done. But then an agent contacted me out of the blue with some deals from Italy. Soon enough, we were packing our bags and moving to Sicily.’

Despite the relative proximity of the two countries, Harper insists Spanish and Italian football could not be more different.

Harper rubbed shoulders with the game's leading lights in Spain, including Cristiano Ronaldo

Zinedine Zidane was just beginning his coaching career during Harper's time at the Bernabeu

‘It’s been a bit of a culture shock,’ he admits. ‘Football in Italy is much more physical. I don’t think I touched a ball for the first ten days of pre-season. It was all about getting fit and not worrying about the technical side of things.

‘It’s different, but that’s why I’m here. I needed to get out of my comfort zone. I feel like I’ve got it all to prove. Nobody really knows me here, I don’t know the language... it’s not easy.

‘But maybe that’s what I need. You know, thirty’s still young. I could have another decade-plus of playing in front of me. So, the plan is to get fit, stay fit and hopefully start climbing the leagues again. The hunger is still there.’

He adds: ‘I’ve kind of been on an opposite journey to a lot of people. I started at a huge club, maybe the biggest club in the world; I’ve had a good contract with a La Liga team; I’ve played in front of my hometown fans and heard them chanting my name. So, I know what it’s like to be there. It doesn’t scare me in the slightest. I’ve had a taste of it and I’m hungry for more.

‘Cristiano Ronaldo has shown how long it’s possible to stay at the top level. So, too, Karim Benzema. Even Harry Kane. What is he now, 33? And he’s just had the best year of his career, winning the Ballon d’Or. It’s not that long ago people were writing forwards off at that age. So, no, I’m still motivated and I don’t see any reason why, with a wee bit of luck, I can’t keep playing until I’m close to my forties.’

If Harper’s self-belief and resilience sound impressive, it’s because he’s had ample opportunity to work on them. In addition to his various injury issues, he’s had to contend with the weight of expectation that comes with being on the books of Real Madrid, intense scrutiny from a very young age, and, of course, plenty of rejection.

Harper moved to Brighton in 2015 but his career failed to take flight with the Seagulls

Perhaps the most memorable example of the latter came in 2015 when he was left out of the Scotland Under-19 squad by then-coach Ricky Sbragia. The former Sunderland boss triggered a backlash from former players, fans and pundits alike when he dismissed Harper as ‘a luxury player’ that his team couldn’t accommodate.

Spanish football journalist Graham Hunter described it as a ‘retrograde, almost prehistoric decision’. Harper’s dad, John, branded the description ‘harsh’, warning that Scotland could lose his son to the Spanish national team.

Sbragia subsequently apologised for his choice of words but Harper admits it took him some time to get over.

‘It was hard to deal with,’ he nods, ‘especially considering the love I have for Scotland. I might have been born in Spain, but I’ve got Scottish blood pumping through me. Honestly, the prospect of playing for Scotland was always more exciting to me than playing for Real Madrid. But that was just the mentality some people had at that time.

‘I was probably the most high-profile victim of that way of thinking but there would have been others as well, players who maybe weren’t as physical and so were written off. But I would definitely say times have changed. You can see that with more technical players like Billy Gilmour coming through and being successful.

‘The game has moved on from that kind of thinking and it’s a good thing, I think, for Scotland that it has.’

Harper, in action for Getafe, has played for a host of Spanish clubs and wanted a new challenge

Whilst his international experience amounts to a handful of age-grade caps, Harper has not yet given up on playing again for his country.

‘The beautiful thing about football is that things can change quickly, especially if you’re a striker. You only need a season or a season and a half of scoring goals, and your career can lift off again. There are so many examples of that, maybe now more than ever.

‘So, that’s the thing that keeps me motivated every day when I go to training. If I can get into a good rhythm, score goals and stay fit, then who knows what might happen? I still have that dream and that hunger to play for Scotland. That might seem a bit crazy to some people. Honestly, sometimes it even seems a bit crazy to me. But it’s the thing that drives me and it’ll continue to drive me either until it happens or I retire.’

Harper admits he would love to experience playing in Scotland before he hangs up his boots, having come close to doing so on multiple occasions in the past.

‘I’ve had phone calls where it’s been like, “Okay, it’s going to get done” and then, for one reason or another, it hasn’t happened,’ he says. ‘I came pretty close to joining St Johnstone one time, and Falkirk as well many years ago. The last couple of years, there’s been interest from some Championship sides. It’s a challenge I’m definitely up for and something I’d like to make happen.’

#2164. Isaksen: “Non nego che ora è un piacere raggiungere il campo di allenamento”

Dall'infortunio alla rinascita con la Lazio: l'esterno danese incorona Gattuso e racconta il suo momento magico tra campo e spogliatoio.

La sosta di novembre vede la Lazio capolista in solitaria in campionato, con un punto di vantaggio sui campioni in carica. Tra i grandi protagonisti di questo avvio di stagione biancoceleste c'è sicuramente l’esterno danese Gustav Isaksen: attuale capocannoniere della Lazio con 4 reti (al pari di Frattesi e Noslin) e fresco erede della fascia da capitano vista l'assenza per infortunio di Zaccagni. Appena arrivato nel ritiro della Danimarca, l‘esterno ha raccontato ai microfoni di sport.tv2.dk il suo momento di grazia e le straordinarie doti tattiche e umane di mister Gattuso.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Ora sono davvero felice, ho trovato la pace interiore sia dentro che fuori dal campo e acquisito più fiducia in me stesso dopo un’estate complessa, tra operazioni e riabilitazione. Il corpo sta rispondendo al meglio e sto riuscendo a dare il mio 100%. Adesso ho un tecnico che vede qualcosa di grande in me e crede nelle mie potenzialità, con Gattuso non devo pensare troppo. Con i precedenti allenatori, anche molto preparati e comunque importanti per la mia crescita, il mio compito era prettamente tattico e difensivo. Ora, invece, devo soltanto seguire il mio avversario in copertura. La nostra strategia mira a difendere in modo da poter subito ribaltare l’azione e attaccare, è questo il modo in cui amo giocare da sempre.

Il mister è un eccellente motivatore, la sua qualità più importante è la capacità di riuscire a tirare fuori il meglio da ogni singolo calciatore. Non nego che ora è un piacere raggiungere il campo di allenamento, nello spogliatoio non vediamo l’ora. Abbiamo tanto riposo, ma quando ci alleniamo è durissima. Si corre come dei pazzi, i ritmi sono elevati e una volta tornati a casa abbiamo tutti bisogno di riposare e dormire. Ma il gruppo funziona alla perfezione ed è fantastico. In questo momento ho fatto il recupero e mi sento bene.

#2163. Lo voleva la Juventus, ora Suzuki è titolarissimo all'Aston Villa. E nessuno rimpiange il Dibu

Zion Suzuki ha lasciato il Parma e l'Italia per accasarsi all'Aston Villa, garantendo un incasso di oltre 30 milioni di euro al club ducale, che ha scelto, come è naturale che sia, di sostituirlo con un giovane promettente come Daffara, che recentemente ha tolto il posto a Corvi. Il giapponese è stato a lungo un obiettivo della Juventus, che ha provato il colpo anche in collaborazione con il PSG, che lo avrebbe mandato in prestito a Torino per poi riprenderlo l'anno seguente.

Unai Emery è abituato a grandi portieri e all'Aston Villa il compito di Suzuki era decisamente arduo perché prima di lui il titolare si chiamava Dibu Martinez, uno dei migliori interpreti del ruolo. Il classe 2002 però non ha tremato, si è preso il posto e ha giocato con la solita tranquillità che lo contraddistingue, sia in Champions, sia in campionato. L'unico incontro che ha saltato è quello perso 3-0 in EFL Cup contro il Bournemouth, mentre il precedente era stato costretto a giocarlo a causa dell'infortunio al 45' di Bizot.

Alla fine si può dire che le parti sono soddisfatte dell'affare estivo: Suzuki è protagonista in una società che ambisce a traguardi importanti, il Parma ha rimpinguato le casse societarie, l'Aston Villa ha preso uno dei top emergenti in porta e la Juventus ha virato su Vicario, che oggi non è certo il problema dei bianconeri. Il prossimo step per lui è puntare ancora più in alto, ma per quello c'è tempo.

#2161. West Ham interested in 22-year-old goalkeeper with minimum $15m transfer fee demanded

West Ham have encountered a goalkeeping dilemma, with Mads Hermansen struggling for form and Alphonse Areola now injured. Attention has turned to the transfer market and potential solutions, and according to Argentine news outlet TyC Sports, WHUFC have eyes on River Plate’s Santiago Beltran.

It is claimed that the Hammers are among the clubs to have shown interest in the 22-year-old, but Spanish giants Atletico Madrid and Premier League side Aston Villa also have eyes on the goalkeeper. River Plate have been keen to extend Beltran’s contract, which expires in 2027, but they are willing to sell if $15m (£11.2m) is tabled.

The Argentine club would be willing to sell in January too, which will suit the Hammers as they look to resolve their goalkeeping issues. Alongside Hermansen and Areola, academy graduate Finlay Herrick is an option available to new boss Scott Parker.

Beltran is a product of the River Plate academy and has broken into the first team setup over the past 18 months. He made his international debut for Argentina in the summer but is also eligible to represent Italy.

Over the course of 2026, Beltran has locked down the starting berth with one of his country’s most prestigious sides. Given that his contract runs out at the end of 2027, it is little wonder that interest from West Ham, Atletico Madrid and Aston Villa is emerging.

In Liga Professional, Argentina’s top flight, Beltran has recorded 50 saves and an xG prevented of 3.93. It shows that while he isn’t necessarily highly active in terms of shot-stopping behind a tight defence, he is doing a lot of individual work to deny goal-bound shots when he is called upon.

He is solid in terms of his short-distance distribution with 259 successful passes, but he has a long ball accuracy of only 27.8%. This is an area of his game to improve, but at only 22, the WHUFC target has plenty of time to grow in this area (all stats via FotMob).

Beltran’s success in Argentina indicates he would be an upgrade on West Ham’s current options. Interest from Atletico Madrid and Aston Villa emphasises the high regard he is held in too.

Importantly, Beltran’s age means that he could become the Hammers’ long-term No. 1. He has both time and room to grow, mainly in his distribution, so he can become an important player off the bat while growing into a valuable financial asset in the years to come.

At around £11m, he wouldn’t be a cheap signing. But, at that price, WHUFC would be signing a goalkeeper upgrade who can only grow in value as he progresses. Beltran feels like a good target and a smart option in the effort to tighten up in goal.

Gennaio si avvicina, così come si scaldano le piste di mercato che portano ai nomi nel mirino delle big (e non solo). Endrick sarebbe il pro­filo giu­sto per la Roma? "È gio­vane ed è del Real Madrid, le qua­lità non gli man­cano. Cono­sco la bot­tega madri­lena e come scel­gono i gio­ca­tori... #2159. Scuole evacuate a Roma dopo nuovi allarmi bomba via email

Tra gli istituti coinvolti figurano il Giovanni Cagliero di Largo Volumnia, il Petrarca di via Ceneda e il Rodari di via Norcia.

Allarme bomba nelle scuole, evacuazioni a Roma: coinvolti numerosi istituti

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Un’unica mail ha fatto scattare un allarme bomba in oltre 100 scuole italiane, provocando evacuazioni e operazioni di bonifica in decine di istituti di ogni ordine e grado. La situazione riguarda anche Roma, dove l’allerta è scattata in numerose strutture.

Nella Capitale sono state interessate diverse scuole del quartiere Appio-Tuscolano. Gli studenti sono stati fatti uscire dagli edifici e sarebbero in corso le operazioni necessarie per trasferirli in luoghi sicuri.

La mail che ha dato origine agli allarmi risulta firmata “Mikhail Andropov”. Al momento sono in corso le evacuazioni.

Secondo quanto riportato da Adnkronos, tra gli istituti romani coinvolti figurano diverse scuole della zona Appio-Tuscolano.

Tra le strutture interessate c’è l’Istituto Comprensivo Giovanni Cagliero, in Largo Volumnia.

L’allarme riguarda anche l’Istituto Petrarca di via Ceneda e l’Istituto Rodari di via Norcia.

Tra gli istituti coinvolti viene indicata inoltre la scuola secondaria di primo grado Sibari, situata nei pressi di Porta Metronia.

L’evacuazione non ha riguardato soltanto questi istituti. Sono state infatti fatte evacuare anche alcune scuole primarie e asili nido della zona.

L’allarme non riguarda esclusivamente Roma. La stessa mail avrebbe infatti interessato oltre 100 scuole in tutta Italia, facendo scattare controlli, bonifiche ed evacuazioni in decine di istituti di ogni ordine e grado.

Nelle scuole romane interessate dall’allerta, gli studenti sono stati allontanati dalle strutture.

Al momento sarebbero in corso le operazioni per il loro trasferimento in luoghi sicuri, mentre proseguono le procedure legate all’allarme.

Una situazione che coinvolge dunque numerosi istituti italiani e che, nella Capitale, interessa in particolare diverse scuole dell’area Appio-Tuscolano.

Doherty, 34, hasn’t played much football for the Blades so far and has been limited to only five appearances in all competitions, three of which have come in the Championship. The Republic of Ireland international, who has made 53 caps for his country to date, has played over 500 games in his career and is vastly experienced.

In this latest update regarding his condition, The Star claim he isn’t too far away from being available again which will be a boost for Chris Wilder’s side. They are back in action after the international break with a home clash against Watford at Bramall Lane.

Sheffield United are positioned in 10th place in the table after 15 fixtures and they are two points off the play-offs behind QPR and Southampton. They were beaten 2-1 away by Charlton Athletic last time out.

Sheffield United could do with having Doherty back following Femi Seriki‘s season-ending injury. He is likely to get plenty of minutes for SUFC over the coming weeks.

Hamza Choudhury can also operate as a full-back as well as midfield if needed. The Blades will get the chance to bolster this particular position in the January transfer window.

Doherty, who is from Dublin, knows the EFL inside out and will be a useful character to have in and around the dressing room. He likes to get up and down the flank and get involved in attacks when necessary.

The veteran has had two separate spells at Wolves in the past. He has also had stints at Tottenham Hotspur and Atletico Madrid so he has some decent pedigree behind him.

Doherty hasn’t got going yet at Sheffield United. SUFC are yet to see the best of the ex-Premier League man.

The Blades snapped him up to bolster their defensive department. He gives them more competition and depth at the back.

Wilder’s men will be eager to return to winning ways against struggling Watford next weekend. The South Yorkshire outfit were disappointed to lose against Charlton Athletic last Saturday and will want to bounce back.

#2156. Fabiani svela la scelta di Gattuso: “Prima opzione, non abbiamo avuto dubbi”

Il ds racconta la scelta di Gattuso: prima opzione di Lazio e Lotito. Poi l’elogio al tecnico della capolista.

Lazio, Fabiani esalta Gattuso: “Sta dirigendo alla grande l’orchestra”

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Gennaro Gattuso era la prima scelta della Lazio. Nessun ripiego e, soprattutto, nessun dubbio da parte del direttore sportivo Angelo Fabiani e del presidente Claudio Lotito. A raccontare i retroscena della scelta dell’allenatore è stato lo stesso dirigente biancoceleste.

Fabiani, parlando della Lazio capolista di Serie A, ha riservato parole importanti a Gattuso. Il ds ne ha sottolineato soprattutto la capacità di rapportarsi con calciatori e dirigenti, utilizzando poi una metafora significativa: “Gli abbiamo dato la bacchetta e lui sta dirigendo alla grande l’orchestra”.

Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, Fabiani ha spiegato innanzitutto quanto sia importante scegliere un tecnico nel momento più adatto: “Gli allenatori sono tutti giusti, ma vanno anche presi al momento giusto”.

L’esperienza maturata nei diversi club della sua carriera ha portato Fabiani a una convinzione precisa sul ruolo dell’allenatore.

“Ne ho avuti tanti nei vari club in cui ho lavorato. Chi non è andato bene è solo perché era arrivato nel momento sbagliato”.

Una situazione che, secondo il direttore sportivo, non riguarda certamente Gattuso. La Lazio aveva infatti individuato subito in Rino il profilo sul quale puntare.

“È stata la nostra prima opzione. Lotito è un presidente che lascia ampia libertà sul mercato, sulla scelta dell’allenatore però è presente”.

Fabiani ha quindi chiarito come la decisione sia stata condivisa con il presidente biancoceleste: “Ma io e lui non abbiamo avuto dubbi nel puntare su Rino. Le sue grandi qualità le conoscevamo bene”.

Il dirigente della Lazio è entrato poi nel dettaglio delle caratteristiche che maggiormente apprezza dell’allenatore.

“Gattuso è stato un campione formidabile, che ha vinto tutto”.

Il valore aggiunto, però, secondo Fabiani va ricercato soprattutto nel modo in cui il tecnico riesce a gestire i rapporti all’interno del club.

“Ma la sua grandezza è mettere tutto questo da parte nel rapporto con i giocatori e con i dirigenti”.

Da qui la frase con cui il direttore sportivo sintetizza il lavoro svolto finora dal tecnico alla guida della Lazio:

“Noi gli abbiamo dato la bacchetta e lui sta dirigendo alla grande l’orchestra”.

#2155. Bayern Munich's £400,000-a-week 'risk' on Harry Kane: Dietmar Hamann reveals doubts about Ballon d'Or winner - and claims no English team would have matched mega contract offer

Published: 17:12 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 17:12 EST, 6 November 2026

Bayern Munich are taking a major 'risk' giving Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane a bumper new deal, according to former midfielder Didi Hamann.

Kane, 33, and Bayern Munich have agreed on a two-year contract extension worth £400,000 per week which will make him the world's highest-paid English sportsman.

But ex-Liverpool and Bayern man Hamann has suggested that this may prove to be a poor move given Kane's age and possible decline.

'Whether he'll still be scoring goals in the coming years, we'll see. He's 33 years old and will be 36 when the contract expires. There's obviously a certain risk involved,' Champions League winner Hamann told Sky Germany.

Hamann then went on to justify his bizarre comments by saying: 'He didn't play well for England at the European Championship two years ago, and he had problems in the last two knockout matches at the World Cup.'

The ex-Germany international also suggested that staying at Bayern was the best deal Kane was going to get at this stage in his career, saying: 'I don't think there were any major suitors from England.

Harry Kane has signed a two-year-long contract extension with Bayern but Didi Hamann is not convinced this is the right move for the Bavarians

Speaking with Sky Germany Dietmar Hamann expressed concerns over his old side offering Kane such a large deal

'They would have taken him for 20 or 30 million, but Bayern would probably have wanted at least half or three-quarters back this summer of the 100 million euros they had to pay Tottenham for Kane in 2023.

'I don't think anyone would have paid that. That's why the contract extension is something they probably couldn't have done any differently.'

Hamann is arguably taking a harsh view on Kane's new deal considering how the Englishman has performed since arriving in Germany.

In three seasons at the Allianz he has 102 Bundesliga goals in as many games as well as 28 assists, winning the Bundesliga Golden Boot every year since his arrival.

The Englishman's goals have fired Bayern to two back-to-back Bundesliga titles and a DFB-Pokal triumph.

But clearly all of this is not enough for Hamann who has previously critiqued Kane's performances in Germany saying that last season his role in Kompany's Bayern side was 'unacceptable.'

In his Sky Germany column the former defensive midfielder wrote: 'I don't know if Kompany is happy that Harry Kane is no longer playing exclusively as a striker.

'It's not acceptable to me that Kane is winning balls in his own penalty area, because that's not his job at all.'

#2153. Che fine ha fatto Hysaj? Retroscena di mercato e futuro ancora in bilico

Successivamente è stato il Bologna a valutare l'albanese per rimpiazzare l'infortunato Holm, ma i rossoblù hanno infine preferito virare su Darmian una volta superati i dubbi di natura fisica su quest'ultimo.

#2152. Bodino (dirigenza Juve): "Vogliamo allenare i leader di domani. C'è l'Europeo..."

Greta Bodino, Chief People, Culture & ESG Officer della Juventus, ha parlato dal palco nel corso del Social Football Summit, che si tiene a Torino all'interno dell'Allianz Stadium.

Ha detto la dirigente della Juve: "Il primo motivo che ci spinge è la volontà di dare una risposta concreta e locale al bisogno di formare nuovi manager, fornendo loro strumenti per governare la complessità. Il secondo tema è la volontà di proporre una formazione sistemica e trasversale. Questo è un percorso volutamente diverso dai tanti master in Sports Management presenti sul mercato: è un master di visione, rigore scientifico e tecnologia, creato per i leader di domani, per insegnare loro a prendere decisioni e a gestire organizzazioni sempre più complesse. Il master è costruito su cinque moduli: pensiero, dati e sistemi; leadership e governance; engagement e comunicazione; sostenibilità; tecnologia e innovazione. Per quanto riguarda la formazione, sarà suddivisa in due parti: lezioni in aula e momenti di confronto, seguiti da un project work concreto".

E ancora, prosegue e conclude Bodino: "Il contributo di Juventus si svilupperà su tre livelli: un advisory board con personalità del club e figure internazionali, le lezioni tenute da alcuni dirigenti e la possibilità di accedere alle infrastrutture. Vogliamo inoltre avere una classe di circa 30 studenti internazionali, che potranno confrontarsi portando le proprie esperienze. L'obiettivo è allenare i leader di domani a comprendere il contesto in cui si trovano, sia internamente sia esternamente, e a sviluppare in modo scientifico la propria capacità decisionale. Pensiamo, per esempio, agli Europei di calcio del 2032, che avranno bisogno di tantissimi professionisti e di una leadership nuova, moderna e più competente".

Birmingham City are top of the table after their first 15 fixtures of the season. BCFC are above Middlesbrough and Stoke City on goal difference following their 2-1 win over Swansea City last time out before the international break.

Attacker Jay Stansfield scored both of the Blues’ goals against the Swans last Saturday. They are back in action with an away trip to Stoke City next weekend.

In the meantime, McAnuff, who played for the likes of Cardiff City, Watford and Reading, has delivered his honest verdict on the Midlands outfit on the latest epiode of BBC’s 72+ Podcast: “Under his (Tom Wagner) guidance, after everything he has put into the club, there is no reason why with such an open start to the league, this could be the season particularly going down to eight teams this year, where they can’t at least get (into the play-offs).

Birmingham City re-signed James Beadle on loan from Brighton and Hove Albion in the summer. BCFC’s goalkeeper is a year older now and is backed up on the bench by Ryan Allsop.

12 NOVEMBRE A NAPOLI L’EVENTO: MEZZOGIORNO, NAPOLI PER L’ALTERNATIVA Sinistra Italiana a Napoli: “Mezzogiorno, Napoli per l’alternativa”. Il 12 novembre al Maschio Angioino il dibattito sul futuro del Sud con Nicola Fratoianni NAPOLI – In un momento storico decisivo per il futuro del Mezzogiorno e del Paese, Sinistra Italiana promuove un appuntamento politico di primario rilievo: l’incontro pubblico dal titolo “Mezzogiorno, Napoli per l’alternativa”, che si terrà giovedì 12 novembre alle ore 17:30 nella prestigiosa cornice della Sala della Loggia presso il Maschio Angioino. L’incontro ha il fine di tracciare una strada chiara per il riscatto sociale ed economico del Sud, mettendo al centro le battaglie storiche per il lavoro, la giustizia sociale, i diritti ed il contrasto alle diseguaglianze territoriali. Presiede: Pietro Rinaldi (R.U. Armena Sviluppo e Responsabile Enti Locali AVS). Modera: Ilaria Urbani (Giornalista de La Repubblica). #2149. Scuole, allarme bomba da Roma alla Toscana: alunni portati fuori

Ad Arezzo i bambini della Tricca sono stati accompagnati al parco Pertini in attesa dei genitori.

Un allarme bomba via email ha raggiunto centinaia di scuole italiane l’11 novembre 2026. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere, Negli istituti che hanno ricevuto la segnalazione anonima, dirigenti e personale stanno facendo uscire gli studenti in via precauzionale, per consentire le verifiche. Gli avvisi riguardano anche Roma, Frosinone e Rieti, oltre a città e province da Nord a Sud.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Nel messaggio si legge: «Ho appena lasciato nel vostro edificio, all'interno di un sacchetto di plastica, un potente ordigno esplosivo con innesco a distanza». La mail è firmata da Mikhail Andropov, che si presenta come «leader del Vilajat del Misoginistan». Si tratta del contenuto della minaccia, non di una presenza di esplosivi accertata.

Una comunicazione di allarme bomba è stata inviata via email a tutte le scuole di Roma. La polizia, contattata dagli istituti, ha indicato di liberare gli edifici con calma. Gli studenti sono tornati nelle proprie abitazioni.

Tra le province in cui risultano segnalazioni figurano anche Frosinone e Rieti. Fuori dal Lazio, gli avvisi sono stati registrati nelle province di Venezia, Trieste, Padova e Brescia, oltre che a Potenza; altre province si stanno aggiungendo all’elenco. Secondo quanto riferisce Corriere, la matrice comune delle email alimenta il sospetto che la minaccia possa essere collegata a un nuovo attacco informatico contro le istituzioni italiane. Nei giorni precedenti circa 200 presidi di scuole di ogni ordine e grado avevano già ricevuto una segnalazione simile.

In Toscana le email minatorie hanno portato a evacuazioni in più province. Tra Firenze e il suo territorio sarebbero cinque gli istituti coinvolti. Altri avvisi riguardano la provincia di Arezzo, con scuole di ogni ordine e grado, dall’infanzia alle superiori, e le province di Siena e Pisa.

Ad Arezzo città i bambini della scuola elementare Tricca sono stati accompagnati al parco Pertini in attesa dei genitori. Sono state evacuate anche la primaria di Staggiano e la scuola materna di Matrignano. Nel Casentino hanno lasciato gli edifici il liceo scientifico Galilei di Poppi e l’Itis Fermi di Bibbiena.

In Versilia, il Comune di Seravezza ha scritto su Facebook: «Una email, arrivata all'Istituto comprensivo, ha annunciato la presenza di un ordigno alla scuola primaria Frediani. Scattate quindi le procedure di evacuazione che hanno interessato sia gli alunni della scuola sia i dipendenti del Municipio».

A Modena è in corso l’evacuazione di almeno cinque istituti superiori e di una scuola primaria. La stessa misura interessa altri due istituti superiori a Vignola e Sassuolo. La polizia locale presidia le scuole coinvolte per garantire la viabilità.

#2147. Martin O'Neill relaxed over Kasper Hogh scoring drought as Celtic boss hails Dane's display against Besiktas

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 17:30 EST, 6 November 2026

Martin O'Neill is adamant that he’s not overly concerned about Kasper Hogh’s goal drought — despite the Dane failing to find the net in 15 matches.

Celtic’s record signing at £11million from Bodo/Glimt, the forward looked set to be a huge hit when he scored a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on August 9 only to go off the boil.

His hopes of ending a barren run against Besiktas on Thursday ended when he was taken off 13 minutes from time, with substitutes Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran climbing off the bench to seal a dramatic 3-2 for O’Neill’s men.

But while O’Neill shared Hogh’s frustration at not getting among the goals again, he made a point of telling him that he should have been proud of his other work on the night.

‘I did, absolutely,’ he explained. ‘I want centre-forwards to be able to hold it and that is what he did.

‘He is not Duran, he is not a dribbler. But if he can do this for us against strong opposition it will stand him in good stead.’

O'Neill admits his record-signing is currently struggling for confidence in front of goal

Hogh hasn't found the net since firing a hat-trick in a 5-1 win over Kilmarnock on August 9

With his player not in the latest Denmark squad, O’Neill believes confidence may be an issue. But he stressed: ‘I think Thursday night will be good for him. I said to him that I’m not worried about whether he scores a goal.

‘Of course, you want centre-forwards to score and, of course, centre-forwards live on them. But I said to him that last night I wanted him to be strong and fight when the ball is played up to him.

'I thought in terms of holding the ball up and bringing people into the game, that he did really well.’

Duran stole the headlines against the Turks, though, with his double securing Celtic’s first win in the Europa League and bringing his personal tally for the season to 13.

‘At this minute, he is on fire,’ O’Neill said of the Colombian. ‘He can play wide right, he has done that. He has played wide left for his other club. But centre forward is where he is dynamic.’

Asked if it was increasingly difficult to start Hogh ahead of Duran through the middle, O’Neill said: ‘We will see. We made five changes on Thursday night because it was necessary.

‘Centre-forwards need a goal but that performance there against European opposition will give him confidence.

‘I don’t know what side we will play on Sunday. But this lad has scored goals in the Champions League remember.

'He will get a confidence boost from Thursday night in terms of doing that part of the game well. But it will be nice for him to score a goal.’

While O’Neill’s side now focus on Kilmarnock, the win over Besiktas has breathed new life into their European campaign. With three points on the board at the midway point, two further wins from their matches with Torreense, Omonia, Marseille and Union Saint-Gilloise may see them qualify for the knockout round.

‘It was really pleasing and really important,’ O’Neill said of Thursday’s dramatic victory. ‘We conceded some ground in the game which was to be expected, but I thought defensively we were really, really strong.

‘From the European side, we have given ourselves a chance. We will have to go and win away from home and it will not be easy. We are looking forward to Sunday and we will look to take it on.’

La Lazio è capolista della Serie A, ma risultati e classifica non rappresentano l’aspetto che rende maggiormente soddisfatto Angelo Fabiani. Il direttore sportivo biancoceleste guarda soprattutto a ciò che è stato costruito all’interno di Formello.

Intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, Fabiani ha parlato del momento vissuto dalla Lazio, del lavoro portato avanti nel corso della propria carriera e anche del suo contratto in scadenza.

Proprio sul futuro il dirigente ha preferito non anticipare nulla, affidandosi però a una frase significativa: “Ne parleremo a tempo debito. Il calcio non è un semplice contratto”.

Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, Fabiani ha spiegato cosa lo rende maggiormente felice dell’attuale momento della Lazio.

La classifica potrebbe rappresentare la risposta più immediata. Il direttore sportivo, invece, guarda oltre i risultati ottenuti sul terreno di gioco.

“Potrei dire i risultati, la classifica. Ma dove arriveremo chi lo sa. La cosa che invece mi rende felice è l’ambiente che si è creato a Formello. Il calcio è alchimia e qui è stata trovata quella giusta”.

Parole che raccontano il momento vissuto dalla Lazio capolista, ma anche l’importanza che Fabiani attribuisce alla costruzione dell’ambiente intorno alla squadra.

Un lavoro che il dirigente biancoceleste ha già affrontato diverse volte nel corso della propria carriera.

“Ho girato l’Italia in lungo e in largo, sempre per ricostruire. Alla Triestina, al Genoa, con il Messina e poi alla Salernitana, dove è iniziato il sodalizio con Lotito. Ora sto cercando di farlo alla Lazio”.

C’è però anche una questione personale ancora da affrontare. Il contratto di Fabiani è in scadenza.

Interrogato sul tema, il direttore sportivo non ha voluto accelerare i tempi né fornire indicazioni su quello che accadrà.

“Ne parleremo a tempo debito. Il calcio non è un semplice contratto”.

Una risposta breve con cui Fabiani rimanda ogni discorso sul proprio futuro. Il presente, intanto, è quello di una Lazio in testa alla Serie A e di un ambiente a Formello che il direttore sportivo considera il vero motivo di soddisfazione di questo momento.

#2145. 200 defensive contributions: Why Blackburn Rovers had to strike new contract deal with one of Mowbray’s ‘soldiers’

Blackburn Rovers have failed when trying to secure the futures of key players in the past. Among the notable names to leave Ewood Park for nothing in years gone by are Ben Brereton Diaz and Tyrhys Dolan, but work is ongoing to change this pattern.

The latest bit of contract business done by Rovers has seen Irish centre-back Sean McLoughlin tied down for the foreseeable. The length of the new deal is undisclosed, but his initial deal was due to expire at the end of the 2026/27 campaign, although a 12-month extension option was in place.

McLoughlin has been a key influence since joining in 2025, and his importance has grown under Tony Mowbray. The boss has spoken about building teams of “soldiers and artists” in the past, and McLoughlin is one of his most important soldiers.

McLoughlin offered Championship experience and leadership abilities in a side that severely lacked both attributes last season. The Irishman captained Blackburn Rovers on multiple occasions in his debut campaign and missed only two of 46 league matches.

The 29-year-old has remained an ever-present this term, playing all 1,350 Championship minutes to date. He has chipped in with one goal and one assist along the way, but his defensive numbers are where he stands out.

No Championship centre-back has recorded more than McLoughlin’s 200 defensive contributions in 15 games so far this season. Watford captain Mattie Pollock equals that impressive tally, but after them, Birmingham City’s Phil Neumann is the closest on 181.

McLoughlin’s 134 clearances is the most of all Championship centre-backs, constantly meeting crosses and attacking deliveries to hoof the danger as far from Balazs Toth‘s goal as possible. His 65 duels won, 40 of them in the air, and 22 blocked shots (top 3%) encapsulate the soldier spirit Mowbray wants from his Rovers defenders.

His wider game deserves praise as well though, showing his passing range with 662 successful passes, 51 accurate long balls and 133 line-breaking passes. McLoughlin reads the game well too, with 31 interceptions ranking him in the top 4% in his position (all stats via FotMob).

The extension option meant McLoughlin’s contract wasn’t a pressing matter. However, the new deal shows proactivity on this front from Blackburn Rovers.

Not only this, but it shows that the former Hull City man is happy at Ewood Park and committed to the task at hand under Mowbray. The hope will be that other valuable players can follow suit and pledge their futures to Rovers.

Todd Cantwell has starred under Mowbray and his deal expires next summer. The same goes for Toth, but the Hungarian goalkeeper continues to rebuff new offers and seems likely to depart in 2027.

The McLoughlin news is positive though, and it will be hoped he can continue to impress in blue and white halves.

#2144. Napoli su Zabi e Tati? Manna: "A volte vengono accostati nomi che non abbiamo mai trattato"

Il Napoli guarda al mercato di gennaio per rinforzare la rosa di Massimiliano Allegri, con particolare attenzione ai giovani talenti. Tra i profili accostati agli azzurri nelle ultime ore ci sono Patrick Zabi, centrocampista classe 2006 del Paris FC, e Tylel Tati, difensore centrale classe 2008 del Nantes. Due prospetti del calcio francese che rispondono all'identikit di calciatori giovani e di prospettiva. Intervenuto ai microfoni di Radio Kiss Kiss Napoli, il direttore sportivo Giovanni Manna ha affrontato il tema delle strategie di mercato, senza confermare l'interesse per i singoli giocatori.

Alla domanda sull'attenzione del Napoli verso la Ligue 1 francese per individuare giovani centrocampisti, Manna ha risposto: “Noi guardiamo tutti i campionati. A volte vengono accostati al Napoli nomi che non abbiamo mai trattato. Fa parte del gioco, perché quando non ci sono notizie di calcio giocato si tende a parlare di mercato, anche facendo nomi che possono creare aspettative non corrette. Cerchiamo un po' di energia, qualcuno che dia freschezza alla squadra, perché è quello che secondo me in questo momento ci sta mancando. Che giochi in Francia, Spagna, Italia o Inghilterra, l'importante è che sia un calciatore interessante. Però dobbiamo prima arrivare a gennaio nel modo migliore”.

#2143. Lazio-Inter, Supercoppa a San Siro: sei cambi possibili nei supplementari

Il regolamento consente fino a cinque sostituzioni nei tempi regolamentari; la sfida è fissata al 22 dicembre alle 21:00.

Inter e Lazio si affronteranno martedì 22 dicembre 2026 alle 21:00 a San Siro per la Supercoppa italiana. La trentanovesima edizione, denominata ufficialmente EA SPORTS FC Supercup, si giocherà in gara unica. La Lega Calcio Serie A ha ufficializzato data, orario, sede e regolamento della partita con un comunicato.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La sfida al Meazza prevede due tempi supplementari da 15 minuti ciascuno se il risultato sarà in parità dopo i 90 minuti regolamentari. Se la parità dovesse persistere, la Supercoppa verrà assegnata ai calci di rigore.

Per la loro esecuzione si applicheranno le modalità indicate nel «Regolamento del Giuoco del Calcio», al paragrafo «Procedure per determinare la squadra vincente di una gara». Inter-Lazio sarà trasmessa in diretta sulle reti Mediaset.

Ciascuna squadra potrà effettuare fino a cinque sostituzioni, utilizzando non più di tre interruzioni di gioco, oltre all’intervallo tra i due tempi. Se si andrà ai supplementari, sarà disponibile una quarta interruzione. Restano inoltre utilizzabili le pause tra la fine dei tempi regolamentari e l’inizio del primo supplementare, e tra il primo e il secondo supplementare.

Solo in caso di tempi supplementari sarà consentito un ulteriore cambio: il limite delle sostituzioni salirà così a sei per squadra.

Il comunicato della Lega disciplina anche le squalifiche di calciatori e tecnici. Chi è in diffida e riceve un’ammonizione nella giornata di campionato precedente la Supercoppa sconterà la squalifica nella successiva gara di campionato. La stessa collocazione è prevista per la squalifica, o per la parte residua della sanzione, di chi viene espulso nella giornata precedente la Supercoppa o ha già una sanzione da scontare; se necessario, il provvedimento riguarderà più gare di campionato.

Anche un calciatore o tecnico già in diffida che venga ammonito durante la Supercoppa sconterà la squalifica nella successiva partita di campionato. Per un’espulsione nella gara del 22 dicembre, la squalifica sarà invece scontata nella gara o nelle gare di campionato successive.

#2142. How Spurs turned their season around: Fiery three-hour meeting before Man United clash, the star who has lit a spark in struggling side and why Rodrigo Bentancur's red card was a key moment

Published: 18:07 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 18:20 EST, 6 November 2026

Choose your Tottenham turning point. The training break in Marbella perhaps. The first win of the season against Coventry, the return of James Maddison, or a rare and emotional victory at Chelsea, only second time in 36 years.

Roberto De Zerbi, the man who has turned the tanker on the pitch, goes instinctively to a heated team meeting before the Manchester United game. It lasted for three hours, from 8pm to 11pm in the team hotel in Manchester city centre.

De Zerbi detected more fire and passion in the meeting room that day and realised change was in the air. He enjoyed hearing home truths exchanged among teammates and between them and his staff members.

'In normal meetings you speak about tactics and mentality,' said De Zerbi. 'In that meeting there was something different. If you are honest in the meeting and you remove the mask and explain your weaknesses a teammate can help you in a difficult moment.

'I believe in people, in relationships, in connections. I don't believe in robots. I don't believe you can come here, put on the shirt and go on the pitch. I believe in the right atmosphere. I love it when I see my players come together to help each other, coming to the stadium even when not selected in the squad. It's crucial.

'Sometimes you can fight but fight for the good of the club not for yourself. Not egoist players but he team, before everything.'

Spurs have won their last three matches having turned the corner under Roberto De Zerbi

Manchester United was the first fixture after the last international break. Spurs were bottom of the Premier League.

They played well at Old Trafford without capitalising, then went behind and had Rodrigo Bentancur sent off for butting Luke Shaw before summoning a fight back, with Dominic Solanke heading in a late equaliser from a cross by Sandro Tonali, the £100million midfielder who finished the game playing at left back.

It provided a spark. Spurs won the next three.

The impact of Bentancur's ban was amplified by Lucas Bergvall's knee injury in the same game. Neither have played since, although Bentancur is available again at Leeds, and De Zerbi reflects positively on the Uruguayan's rush of blood.

'Very important,' said the Spurs boss. 'I don't know if without that red card the reaction would have been like this, but the reaction was good because sometimes we are afraid to show more passion.

'I like people to say Tottenham played well but I want people to say Tottenham played with passion. That they were strong and helped each other on the pitch. That they had hot blood inside. That they played for the club and the fans. My dream is to hear people talk like this.'

Without Bentancur and Bergvall, De Zerbi flexed into a 352 formation against Coventry. Maddison started his first game for nearly 18 months and Spurs won for the first time this season, then disappeared on secretive training break for four nights in Marbella.

They were back in a familiar 4231 shape against Chelsea with Mateus Fernandes starting for the first time since he had been hooked at half time against Aston Villa and criticised by De Zerbi.

Fernandes was the best player on the pitch and clicked with Tonali and the pair excelled again against Crystal Palace.

For all the best laid plans, some good things can happen by chance.

Rodrigo Bentancur's red card in the draw with Man United has proved a key moment for Spurs

Back in August, in the aftermath of a 2-0 defeat by Newcastle in the first home game of this season, Tonali stood near the dressing rooms in conversation with club owners Vivienne Lewis and her son-in-law Nick Beucher.

Tonali was disconsolate. The new Spurs regime had invested a club record fee to sign him at the behest of De Zerbi but he was sluggish, miles from his best and had just been given the runaround by Nico Gonzalez, the player bought to replace him for half the price.

His body language was apologetic, and the owners appeared keen to offer some words of encouragement as they bid farewells and took a lift to the corporate suites in the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Two months on, the Italian has hit his stride. He has been dominant in the last two games. Sharper in mind, more decisive and quicker across the ground. Reading play, breaking things down, covering the miles. He looks like an elite midfielder.

'To play well, Tonali has to run and to work on the pitch,' said De Zerbi before hinting at more to come from Fernandes. 'Mateus is showing 50-60 per cent of his potential,' said the Spurs boss.

For all the rhetoric about unity, the return of Maddison has reset the creativity levels. His presence lifted the crowd and had a similar effect on his teammates. Possession is more secure. His quality on the ball gives others time to organise and with him Spurs look a lot more like scoring a goal. Passes fizz around at a brisker tempo and he carries threat from around the fringes of the penalty box. The goal he swept into the top corner to open the scoring against Coventry was exquisite.

Sandro Tonali has become a vital player for De Zerbi after a mixed start to his Tottenham career

Mo Kudus is back and Dejan Kulusevski's return after so long lifted morale. Less obvious is the return of Dominic Solanke, a genuine centre forward who can operate with his back to goal and bring others into play. Solanke has helped the team gel even if his goal return remains disappointing and De Zerbi admits he and Omar Marmoush are suffering low confidence.

After being criticised for ignoring the club's academy talent, De Zerbi has tried to integrate Luca Williams-Barnett. He cannot talk about togetherness if he refuses to engage with one significant arm of the club. Williams-Barnett made his Premier League debut as a sub against Palace. De Zerbi claimed he thought about starting him at Chelsea and urged the 18-year-old attacking midfielder to learn from those around him.

'The young player has to remove all social media and stay focused on improvement,' said De Zerbi. 'They have to follow the older teammates with more experience and work hard. Expectation and hype is normal. He can become a top player and has to get used to strong pressure and high expectation.'

Win at Leeds on Saturday and Spurs will go into another international break in touch with the top five. It has been quite a turnaround and chief executive Vinai Venkatesham popped up on a podcast this week talking about ambitions to win the Premier League title.

'Great to hear,' said De Zerbi. 'The first thing for people in this club is to be ambitious but to be ambitious you have to show the right mentality every day, game by game because words are not enough.

'What Vinai, the Lewis family and Johan Lange are doing is something special. In the last two seasons you can see they are changing a lot of things in this club. For me as coach, my staff and the players, we have to show we have the self to stay in this club.

'With the right behaviour, the right mentality, to be angry every day and to make a result. This is the best thing to do from our side.'

#2141. EFL expert Jobi McAnuff backs ‘fantastic’ Middlesbrough as Championship promotion favourites

Middlesbrough are winless in their last two games against Wrexham and Watford. They drew 0-0 with the latter last time out at Vicarage Road before the international break.

Boro are sat joint-top of the Championship table after 15 fixtures along with Birmingham City and Stoke City. They are behind the Blues on goal difference.

McAnuff, who played for the likes of Cardiff City, Watford and Reading, has delivered his verdict on Kim Hellberg‘s side on BBC’s 72+ Podcast: “Middlesbrough are a fantastic team. I love what Kim Hellberg has done. It’s amazing isn’t it, for such a good team, so well functioning around the striker (Will Lankshear), you take him out and he’s been phenomenal this season, what an impact that can have.

“That was a little bit the issue last season, not having that real killer at the top end of the pitch to take those half chances, getting in that position. They’ve missed him the last couple (of games). I still have them for sure as my favourites. I think anyone who is above them this year will be getting automatically promoted.”

Middlesbrough sold key man Hayden Hackney to Everton in the summer. Boro also got money from a sell-on clause they had on Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa to Chelsea.

They reinvested heavily into their playing squad following their play-off final defeat to Hull City at Wembley back in May. The likes of Will Lankshear, Ashley Phillips and Radek Vitek came through the entrance door at the Riverside Stadium.

Lankshear, 21, has been prolific under the guidance of Hellberg and has scored 15 league goals already. However, he has missed the last two outings against Wrexham and Watford due to injury and his presence has been missed.

The ex-Tottenham Hotspur will be hoping to return after the international break against Bristol City at home. His team haven’t managed to score without him which is a big worry.

Middlesbrough can’t just rely solely on Lankshear. They need others like David Strelec and Kyle Joseph to step up.

The latter was snapped up from Hull City in early July. He hasn’t managed to score yet in the league and has found it hard to find his shooting boots.

Boro have been strong overall this term and will fancy their chances of finishing in the top two. Hellberg is an impressive young manager and as McAnuff alluded to, his team are well drilled and tough to play against.

They have some solid players like Aidan Morris, Amario Cozier-Duberry and Riley McGree and on their day, they are a match for anyone in the second tier. Hellberg’s men will be eager to return to winning ways against Bristol City next up and their upcoming opponents have been struggling for form of late.

Middlesbrough will get the chance to freshen up their squad in January with some new faces. They will also have the opportunity to let some players leave if needed.
