#2140. Ronaldinho torna in campo, parla l'ultimo che l'ha visto giocare: "È ancora di un'altra categoria"

"La classe, quella, non si perde mai". Parola di Cristian Zaccardo, uno che Ronaldinho lo ha appena ritrovato dall'altra parte del campo. Nell'amichevole di Zurigo tra Del Piero & Friends e Ronaldinho & Friends, il campione del mondo 2006 lo scorso 6 novembre si è ritrovato infatti faccia a faccia con uno dei talenti più straordinari della storia del calcio. E il piacere di rivederlo è stato reciproco: "Sempre un piacere rivederti", ha scritto Zaccardo sui social, accompagnando il messaggio con una fotografia insieme al Gaucho. Un incontro tra vecchie glorie che ha riportato tutti indietro nel tempo. Ma quello, per Ronaldinho, era solo un allenamento pre-partita.

A 46 anni, il brasiliano nelle prossime ore tornerà infatti a indossare gli scarpini con la maglia del Ravenna, nel derby contro il Forlì al Bruno Benelli. Ma in quali condizioni si trova oggi dopo ben undici anni dalla sua ultima partita da professionista? Lo abbiamo chiesto, in esclusiva per TMW, proprio a Zaccardo: "Ronaldinho è sempre Ronaldinho. Magari non ha più vent'anni, però appena prende palla si vede subito che è di un'altra categoria. Ha ancora la giocata, ha ancora il sorriso, ha ancora quella leggerezza che solo lui ha". Insomma, il piede è rimasto quello di sempre. Gli anni possono aver cambiato il fisico, ma non cancellano certe magie.

C'è però un interrogativo che accompagna questo ritorno e sul quale lo stesso ex difensore, oggi agente, si interroga senza nascondere la curiosità: la forma fisica. "Se giocherà con i ragazzi più giovani, si sente, non sarà facile fisicamente. Sono molto curioso di vedere come reggerà sotto il profilo atletico. E quanto reggerà? Quindici minuti, un tempo, sessanta? La classe è sempre la stessa". Una domanda che troverà finalmente risposta sul prato del Benelli. Nessuno pretende di rivedere il ragazzo che faceva impazzire il Camp Nou o San Siro, ma anche un solo lampo del vecchio Gaucho potrebbe valere il prezzo del biglietto.

#2139. Lazio, Fabiani: “A gennaio non parte nessuno”. Poi sorprende su Floriani

Il ds blinda la rosa per gennaio e, tra i protagonisti della Lazio, indica Floriani: “Ci credevamo, ora sta mostrando chi è”.

Lazio, Fabiani: “A gennaio non parte nessuno”. Poi sorprende su Floriani

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Nessuno lascerà la Lazio durante il mercato invernale. A garantirlo è il direttore sportivo biancoceleste Angelo Fabiani, che chiude così la porta a possibili partenze a gennaio nonostante la crescita del valore della rosa.

Il lavoro sul mercato e quello svolto da Gattuso hanno infatti aumentato in maniera esponenziale il valore dei giocatori della Lazio capolista della Serie A. Una situazione che potrebbe inevitabilmente attirare l’attenzione di altri club.

Fabiani, però, non sembra avere alcun dubbio sulle intenzioni della società. E quando gli viene chiesto di scegliere, tra Frattesi, Tavares, Taylor, Belahyane, Noslin e Isaksen, il colpo del quale va maggiormente fiero, il ds sorprende indicando un altro nome: Floriani.

Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, il direttore sportivo della Lazio ha affrontato entrambi gli argomenti nel corso dell’intervista concessa al quotidiano.

La crescita della rosa biancoceleste potrebbe aumentare inevitabilmente l’interesse nei confronti dei calciatori della Lazio. Fabiani riconosce quanto sia aumentato il loro valore, ma esclude possibili “scippi” durante la prossima finestra di mercato.

“Che adesso i giocatori valgano molti di più è un dato di fatto. Ma nel mercato invernale non andrà via nessuno, questo lo posso garantire”.

Parole nette da parte del direttore sportivo. La Lazio, dunque, secondo quanto garantito da Fabiani, non perderà nessuno dei suoi giocatori durante il mercato di gennaio.

A Fabiani vengono poi sottoposti diversi nomi: Frattesi, Tavares, Taylor, Belahyane, Noslin e Isaksen. La domanda è semplice: di quale colpo va più fiero?

Il direttore sportivo parte però da un’esperienza precedente alla Lazio: “Di Napoli, che presi al Messina. Voleva smettere, è diventato Re Artù”.

Quando il discorso si sposta specificamente sulla Lazio, la scelta ricade invece su Floriani.

“Come Lazio dico Floriani. Non è un acquisto, ma un ragazzo che abbiamo cresciuto, mandato a giocare con il premio di valorizzazione perché ci credevamo e ora sta mostrando chi è”.

Una risposta significativa, soprattutto considerando i nomi proposti nella domanda. Fabiani non sceglie uno degli acquisti indicati, ma punta su un giocatore cresciuto dalla Lazio e nel quale, come sottolineato dallo stesso direttore sportivo, il club aveva deciso di credere.

#2138. Zero goals in seven games: Ex-Sheffield Wednesday man struggles for form after stern ‘good riddance’ exit message

Sheffield Wednesday rebuilt their squad in the summer, with a brand-new group of players put together after multiple departures. Among those to move on was striker Ike Ugbo, who joined Cypriot side Apollon Limassol on an initial season-long loan after two goals in 62 games as a permanent SWFC player.

Ugbo’s move was viewed as a much-needed one for all parties, and former administrator Kris Wigfield didn’t hesitate to make his feelings known upon the deal. He wrote in a since-deleted X post: “When even in the bleakest of financial circumstances, a high wage earner shows such entitlement for the money they receive and such contempt for the supporters that were literally paying his wages – you have no chance. Good riddance.”

Ugbo defended himself before turning his attention to the next chapter in his career. A move to Cyprus marked a chance for the 28-year-old to rediscover his past best, but he has struggled to hit the ground running.

Ugbo scored only twice in two seasons after earning a permanent move to Sheffield Wednesday. His initial loan under Danny Rohl was a major success as his seven goals helped inspire the Owls to Championship survival.

Unfortunately, such success has proven tough to emulate, and that has been the case with Apollon Limassol too. Ugbo has made seven appearances – all from the bench – and failed to find the back of the net.

He played in their UEFA Conference League third-round qualifier and his other six outings have come in the league. Apollon Limassol were unbeaten in the first eight matches before a 1-0 loss to Olympiakos Nicosia last weekend.

Ex-SWFC man Ugbo’s battle to break into the starting XI has been made tougher by the form of fellow summer signing Alen Ozbolt, who has seven goals in 11 games from striker. Wingers Brandon Thomas (five goals, three assists) and Garry Rodrigues (four goals, five assists) have impressed too.

Ugbo is still searching for form in Cyprus, and Sheffield Wednesday are hoping a new talisman emerges too.

Jamal Lowe has seven goals in 15 games having made a strong start to the season, but form has waned in recent weeks and he served a three-match suspension for a red card against Notts County on October 20th.

Davis Keillor-Dunn has found more minutes and now has five goals in 13 appearances. Among those hoping to come up with more consistent goalscoring returns for new SWFC boss Dave Challinor are Mason Burstow, Ali Al-Hamadi and Harry Gray.

The unlocking of a truly prolific goalscorer will be key if the Owls are to cement themselves as strong promotion candidates in League One.

#2136. Lazio, Piazza della Libertà cambia volto: conclusa la grande riqualificazione

Conclusa la riqualificazione del giardino: nuovi viali, pavimentazione e un'area sportiva nel luogo dove nacque la Lazio.

Lazio, rinasce Piazza della Libertà: nuovo volto per il luogo dove tutto ebbe inizio

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Piazza della Libertà cambia volto e torna a valorizzare uno dei luoghi più significativi della storia della Lazio. Sono terminati gli interventi di riqualificazione e abbellimento del giardino della piazza nella quale, nel 1900, nacque la Società Podistica Lazio.

Oggi, mercoledì 11 novembre, alle ore 13, si è svolto l'incontro tra il Primo Municipio di Roma Capitale e la Fondazione S.S. Lazio 1900 ETS per presentare i lavori conclusi. Nuovi viali, pavimentazione e un'area attrezzata per lo sport restituiscono un volto rinnovato a uno dei salotti più nobili della Città Eterna.

Una giornata dal significato ancora più profondo per il mondo biancoceleste. Proprio l'11 novembre 2007 moriva Gabriele Sandri, tifoso laziale. Per mantenerne vivo il ricordo, la famiglia ha fortemente voluto la nascita della Fondazione Gabriele Sandri, realtà che proprio da Piazza della Libertà ha dato vita a numerose iniziative sociali e benefiche nel nome di Gabriele.

Secondo quanto riportato dalla Fondazione S.S. Lazio 1900 ETS, la conclusione degli interventi rappresenta un nuovo passo nel percorso di valorizzazione di un luogo indissolubilmente legato alla storia biancoceleste.

È proprio da Piazza della Libertà che ebbe inizio un'avventura lunga ormai oltre 126 anni. Una storia che nel tempo ha attraversato campi di gioco, piscine, fiumi e laghi, parquet dei palazzetti, piste degli stadi, cieli e montagne. Ovunque fosse possibile praticare sport, lì è arrivata la Lazio.

I lavori sono stati realizzati attraverso risorse PNRR, nell'ambito del progetto Caput Mundi, gestito dal Ministero del Turismo e la cui attuazione è stata affidata alla Struttura commissariale per il Giubileo 2025. Gli interventi hanno interessato diverse zone del giardino con l'obiettivo di aumentarne fruibilità, accessibilità e qualità urbana.

Sono stati costruiti tre nuovi viali. Il primo collega via Cesi con l'interno del giardino. Il secondo attraversa la zona centrale dell'area in direzione del viale interno già esistente, mentre il terzo conduce verso la Torretta della Fondazione S.S. Lazio 1900 ETS.

È stata inoltre realizzata la pavimentazione dello spazio che circonda la Torretta lungo i tre lati rivolti verso il giardino. Nell'area centrale sono state posizionate anche due lastre di travertino, utilizzate per la copertura e il livellamento dello spazio.

Particolare attenzione è stata riservata allo sport. Sul lato del giardino rivolto verso Ponte Regina Margherita è nata una nuova area attrezzata. Sono state installate una struttura calistenica con barre per le trazioni e panca, collocata su una pavimentazione antitrauma, oltre a una struttura bikefit.

All'incontro hanno preso parte l'assessore municipale Stefano Marin e i rappresentanti della Fondazione S.S. Lazio 1900 ETS.

Grande soddisfazione è stata espressa da Marco Chiarion Casoni, presidente della Fondazione S.S. Lazio 1900 ETS.

«Siamo orgogliosi e felici che Piazza della Libertà, sede della nascita e parte fondamentale della storia della nostra Società, sia stata interessata da un intervento così importante – dichiara Casoni –. La riqualificazione, il rinnovamento degli spazi e la presenza di nuove attrezzature sportive restituiscono alla piazza una maggiore qualità e una nuova capacità di essere vissuta dalla cittadinanza».

Il percorso, tuttavia, non si fermerà con la conclusione di questi lavori.

«Ma il progetto di valorizzazione non finisce qui – aggiunge Casoni –. Insieme al Primo Municipio stiamo lavorando per continuare ad abbellire e valorizzare Piazza della Libertà. Per noi è particolarmente significativo poter contribuire alla cura di un luogo nel quale, 126 anni fa, è iniziata la storia della Lazio. Ringraziamo le istituzioni e l'architetto Romolo Crescenzi per il lavoro svolto e per aver reso possibile questa evoluzione».

Soddisfazione anche da parte del Municipio Roma I Centro. L'assessore Stefano Marin ha sottolineato il valore dell'intervento per la città e per il territorio.

«Ringrazio la Fondazione S.S. Lazio 1900 ETS per la collaborazione e tutti coloro che hanno contribuito alla realizzazione di questi interventi. Piazza della Libertà è un luogo importante per la storia sportiva e per la vita del nostro territorio. Siamo felici di restituire ai cittadini uno spazio più bello, accessibile e vivibile», dichiara Marin.

Una Piazza della Libertà rinnovata, dunque, ma sempre profondamente legata alle proprie radici. Proprio lì dove, 126 anni fa, iniziò la storia della Lazio.

#2134. ‘We are concerned’: Aribim Pepple among triple Plymouth Argyle injury worries ahead of Sheffield Wednesday tie

Plymouth Argyle sit 5th in the League One table coming into this weekend’s clash with Sheffield Wednesday. It marks an important game for PAFC given their opponents are also in the promotion conversation, but Tom Cleverley and co have a new trio of injuries to deal with.

Speaking to The Herald, the Pilgrims boss revealed muscle injuries are casting doubt over the availability of Aribim Pepple, Alex Mitchell and Michael Baidoo. Cleverley said: “We are concerned with a few of them. We have had a good result tonight and whatever team we take to Sheffield on Saturday we will have full confidence that it can go and do a job and get a win.”

Cleverley later described Pepple and Mitchell specifically as “major doubts”. If they are indeed sidelined, they will join Julio Pleguezuelo as a recent injury blow having damaged his calf in training last week.

Centre-back Mitchell is a powerful figure in defence and a mainstay for Cleverley. He will be a miss for Plymouth Argyle, but there is the depth to deal with his absence with Mathias Ross and Alex Hartridge both available.

Baidoo meanwhile has been building towards his comeback, so a setback comes as a blow. When fully fit, there is intrigue over whether he can grow into an influential player for Cleverley after a tough time at Home Park since joining in January 2025.

Of the three though, Pepple is the most influential. The Canadian striker is PAFC’s leading goalscorer and main attacking threat, offering excellent finishing and link-up ability as a powerful figure at the top of the pitch.

Losing his clinical finishing and ability to lead the line will be a big blow against Sheffield Wednesday. It will be hoped that Pepple is not facing a long spell out, as it will leave a sizeable gap in the frontline to fill.

Cleverley will be forced into changes from his usual lineup if Pepple and Mitchell are ruled out. He has the depth to deal with the absences, although the Plymouth Argyle side is undoubtedly weaker without them.

In defence, the earlier mentioned Alex Hartridge or Mathias Ross could come into the team. Wes Harding has mainly been used at full-time this term but the vice captain can be used centrally if Cleverley wishes.

At striker, it depends on the setup Cleverley opts for. Will Evans seems bound to start either way, but if he wants to partner him with another forward in a 4-4-2, Owen Oseni may be introduced after his recent comeback from injury.

Oliver Irow has been played up front before too, so the PAFC boss has decisions to make.

#2132. England star Ollie Watkins' wife Ellie seeks sanctuary back in the UK amid missile attacks in Saudi Arabia

Published: 09:41 EST, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 04:37 EST, 7 November 2026

England striker Ollie Watkins' wife Ellie has sought sanctuary back in the United Kingdom, seeking 'normality' for their children amid missile attacks in Saudi Arabia in the Middle East conflict.

Ollie and Ellie, 31 and 30, moved to Saudi capital Riyadh in the summer with their two children after a £51million transfer from Aston Villa to Al-Hilal. But the recent deadly re-escalation of the Houthi-Saudi Arabia conflict has sparked concerns. And Ellie and the children have moved back temporarily 'until it calms down'.

The Watkins family have two young children - Amara, five, and three-year-old Marley. Ellie initially admitted she had broken down in tears over the move but later felt 'everything was coming together'.

'We've had a bit of a plot twist,' Ellie said in a post on TikTok today. 'I have come back to the UK for, hopefully, a little bit. I don't actually know when.'

Major airports in Saudi Arabia are operating reduced services after a missile attack by Yemen's Houthi movement on Riyadh's airport killed 13 people. Two people were also killed after an attack at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.

'There's just a little bit of conflict and things going on over in Saudi and we basically decided just to stay here until it calms down,' Ellie added.

Ollie Watkins and wife Ellie moved to Saudi Arabia following his £50m summer transfer (Source: Instagram/Ellie Watkins)

Ellie has now returned to the UK amid missile attacks in Saudi (Source: Instagram/Ellie Watkins)

'I felt like I needed to do that for the kids so there is some form of normality until we can get back out there and all be together.'

Husband Ollie is hoping for a call-up to the England squad this week and will continue to play in the Saudi Pro League while his family reside in the UK.

Saudi football experts have suggested the striker, who has five goals and five assists in eight Saudi Pro League appearances so far, earns 'a minimum of £20million a year' - tax-free.

Al-Hilal play Shabab AlAhli, of Dubai, in the Asian Champions League today.

Ollie and Ellie have been settling into a new home, redecorating and finding schools for their children in Riyadh.

Meanwhile, football's 2027 Asia Cup has been delayed by almost a year amid the ongoing Middle East crisis. The Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition event has also been called off while Formula One is expected to move its end-of-season races.

Ellie had said moving to Saudi Arabia has 'been a lot' but 'everything's finally coming together' - posting photos of their new life together (Source: Instagram/Ellie Watkins)

The WAG shared a snap of their stylish living room as she added: 'Everything's finally coming together and we're so happy in our new home' (Source: Instagram/Ellie Watkins)

Less than two months before it was due to kick off, the Asia Cup was today postponed until December 2027.

It makes the tournament not only a logistical nightmare for the 24 participating teams but also raises serious safety concerns.

A statement from the Asian Football Confederation said: 'The Organising Committee for AFC Asian Cup approved rescheduling the flagship national team tournament considering the current exceptional circumstances arising from developments in the region, including substantial logistical complexities and travel disruptions.

'The new dates of the tournament (December 23 2027 to January 21 2028) will be presented to FIFA for approval.

'Exceptional circumstances have been created for the organisation and delivery of the Competition as originally scheduled, making the postponement necessary in the interest of all participating teams, officials, spectators and other stakeholders.'

However, the delay boosts several Premier League clubs, who no longer face losing players for up to a month of the season. Japan had ten Premier League players available for selection, with Aston Villa potentially losing first-choice goalkeeper Zion Suzuki.

#2131. Tom Brady issues farewell message to ‘special’ Birmingham City after unceremonious exit

Birmingham City announced on Monday that Tom Brady‘s involvement with the club had come to an end. He arrived as part of Knighthead’s investment group upon the takeover in 2023 and featured in the advisory board at BCFC.

However, he was not heavily involved in football decisions and, barring the Amazon documentary ‘Built in Birmingham: Brady & The Blues’, he wasn’t a particularly prevalent figure at St Andrew’s and attended only four games in total. It meant that, despite his public profile, a brief social media statement made for quite an unceremonious exit.

Now, Brady has issued his goodbyes on his Instagram story. He took the chance to thank all those involved in his time at a ‘special’ Birmingham City, stating he’ll be rooting for the club as their journey continues after his departure.

Writing on his Instagram story, Brady said:

“Being part of Birmingham City Football Club the last three years has been one of the most rewarding journeys of my life.

“Thank you to the players, Chris Davies and his staff, the front office, and to everyone working behind the scenes, whose commitment I saw up close at every level of the club.

“Most of all, thank you to the people of Birmingham. Your passion, your loyalty, and the way you show up for this club through every high and every hard day are what make it so special. I’ll always be rooting for your success.”

The message shows Brady’s sentiment towards the club and appreciation of the supporters’ backing throughout his three years. However, the fact his close associate and friend Tom Wagner was not mentioned raises some eyebrows. Perhaps it was just an inadvertent omission, but it still comes as a surprise.

Tom Brady is a recognised name around the world, so his involvement with Birmingham City quickly brought attention. His prevalence in their Amazon documentary perhaps indicated his influence at St. Andrew’s would be more significant.

The former American football star’s profile and the attention he brought certainly plays a part in his legacy. Brady’s presence no doubt brought more eyes from a wider audience to BCFC, aiding from a commercial perspective.

Brady’s friend and body coach Alex Guerrero joined an overhauled medical department, which has decreased injuries. This and his commercial value make up his legacy, but the rather abrupt exit perhaps shows that his lasting mark at Birmingham City isn’t particularly significant – especially in comparison to the likes of Wagner and Davies.

#2130. Man United fans urge supporters to REFUSE to buy booze at Old Trafford as groups ramp up anti-Glazer and Sir Jim Ratcliffe protests ahead of Sunday's clash with Aston Villa

Published: 04:44 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 04:49 EST, 7 November 2026

Manchester United fan groups are calling for a booze boycott at Sunday’s game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford as part of their protests against the club’s owners.

Supporters have revived the green and gold campaign against the Glazer family in recent weeks, with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe also in their sights.

During Tuesday’s Champions League win over Roma at Old Trafford, green and gold balloons were released from the Stretford End before kick-off and tennis balls were thrown onto the pitch in the 20th minute.

Now groups including Reclaim the Stretford End, The 1958, The Red Army, Manchester United Youth Supporters’ Club, South Stand United and Retro Reds are urging fans to hit the owners in the pocket by refusing to buy alcohol in the stadium at the Villa game.

Supporters have been asked to release balloons again when the teams come out before the match, but to respect the minute’s silence on Remembrance Sunday.

The joint organisers say they are protesting against the ownership, the plans to knock down Old Trafford and build a new 100,000-seater stadium next door, United’s debts of more than £1billion, and what they say is a decline in standards throughout the club and the disrespect being shown to match-going fans.

Manchester United supporter groups have urged fans to follow an alcohol boycott

Fan groups are ramping up protests against the Glazer family and co-owners INEOS

Details of the new protest have emerged after it was confirmed that three people were arrested for throwing tennis balls onto the pitch during the Roma game. The game had to be halted temporarily as the players helped to remove them.

Greater Manchester Police made a further eight arrests including four for assault, two for public order offences, one for fraud and one for possession of Class B drugs.

But the game passed off without the serious trouble that has marred previous meetings between United and Roma dating back to their first meeting in the quarter-final of the Champions League in April 2007 when Italian riot police were widely criticised for wading into English fans after they reacted to being pelted with missiles by Roma supporters.

United famously won the return leg 7-1 when police made 18 arrests after fans clashed outside Old Trafford.

#2129. Dave Challinor facing Barry Bannan situation already at Sheffield Wednesday

Bethany Patrick is a football writer based in Manchester, UK.

Her work focuses on the EFL, with particular interest in football governance, supporter culture, and fan experience and access.

Bethany is a director of the award-winning Sheffield Wednesday Women’s Supporters Group, where she works on fan engagement, strategy and campaigns for greater inclusion across the game.

She regularly represents supporters in governance spaces across Europe, including government panels and discussions around football regulation and the supporter's voice.

She has previously worked as a researcher for The Stretford Paddock and is a regular contributor to The Wednesday Week.

Dave Challinor has a big decision to make over Barry Bannan's role at Sheffield Wednesday, with growing numbers of supporters questioning whether the midfielder should remain an automatic starter.

Bannan returned to Hillsborough from Millwall in the summer as one of 18 new additions, with the experienced midfielder expected to play a major role in Wednesday's bid to secure a return to the Championship.

However, the 36-year-old has struggled to consistently reach the standards supporters have come to expect, and Sunday's 2-1 FA Cup defeat to Oldham Athletic has intensified the debate around his place in the starting XI.

For new manager Challinor, it is an early selection dilemma that could prove significant in shaping his Wednesday side.

Challinor has already made clear that he sees Bannan as an important part of his plans at Hillsborough.

Speaking before the Oldham tie, the Owls boss identified central midfield as the Scot's best position, explaining that he wants him to control matches, dictate play and use his passing range to bring attacking players into the game.

He even compared Bannan to Oliver Norwood, who enjoyed considerable success under Challinor at Stockport County despite being in the latter stages of his playing career.

There is little doubt that Bannan still possesses qualities that are valuable to this Wednesday squad, particularly given his experience and understanding of what it takes to get out of League One.

However, there is a difference between being an important member of the squad and being guaranteed a place in the starting XI.

Wednesday's performance at Oldham exposed several problems, and Bannan was among those who struggled to impose themselves on the contest.

With Challinor demanding greater physical intensity and consistency, the midfielder may need to adapt his role as the season progresses.

Sheffield Wednesday were defeated by League Two opposition in Dave Challinor's first game as manager

The reaction from Wednesday supporters suggests frustration with Bannan goes beyond Sunday's defeat, with questions being raised about his declining influence and whether he still warrants an automatic starting place.

One questioned why the midfielder no longer seems capable of taking games by the scruff of the neck, pointing to a perceived drop-off in his longer passing and creative output.

Others have been more direct, believing Bannan should have to earn his place back in the side, while fans have also questioned whether he can still cope with the physical demands of playing regularly.

Some were even more critical, suggesting Bannan's return to Hillsborough had been a mistake.

There is a clear theme emerging: supporters are not necessarily questioning Bannan's importance to the club, but believe his performances this season have not justified the preferential treatment his status might afford him.

It would be premature to write Bannan off entirely, particularly given the circumstances surrounding Wednesday's season and the number of changes made to the squad.

At 36, he is approaching the twilight of his playing career, but his experience could prove invaluable in helping Challinor establish the standards and culture he wants at Hillsborough.

Should Challinor drop Bannan for Saturday's game against Plymouth Argyle? Comment your opinion below!

Michael Storch has already spoken positively about the possibility of Bannan remaining at Wednesday beyond his playing days, potentially moving into coaching or another role at the club.

For now, though, the priority is getting the best out of him on the pitch.

Challinor has inherited a struggling side and cannot afford to select players based on reputation alone.

Bannan has earned enormous respect through his contribution to Wednesday, but that cannot exempt him from the same standards as everybody else.

#2128. Sunderland and Wolves have dodged ‘£10m’ QPR transfer bullet

Queens Park Rangers head into the international break in the eighth and final play-off spot in the Championship, as Julien Stephan looks to cement his side's place in the top third of the league throughout the course of the campaign.

QPR have quietly emerged as serious play-off contenders in the first third of the Championship season, as, with six wins, six draws, and three defeats in the opening 15 games, the R's have looked a tricky opponent.

The West London outfit managed to avoid any major losses over the summer whilst drastically improving the squad for pennies, bringing in the likes of Dennis Cirkin, Tariq Lamptey, Glenn Kamara, Boy Kemper, and Pierce Charles.

The play-offs look to be a real prospect this season, though that may not have been the case had they lost one of their key assets amid Premier League interest.

25-year-old striker Rumarn Burrell joined QPR for around £1 million in the summer of 2025 from League One Burton Albion, having scored 11 and assisted twice in 30 third-tier games for the Brewers.

Spending time with Grimsby Town, Middlesbrough, Bradford City, Kilmarnock, Falkirk, and Cove Rangers before his one season with Burton, Burrell has gone from strength to strength at Loftus Road, scoring ten and assisting three in 30 Championship games in his first season in the English capital.

The Jamaican international has not gone under the radar as QPR would have hoped, as, according to FootballInsider, the likes of Sunderland, Wolverhampton Wanderers, and AFC Bournemouth were monitoring his situation over the summer.

However, no bid was officially confirmed to have been launched, as Burrell remained at Loftus Road; now, those clubs may be breathing sighs of relief.

Football League World has asked AI to rank the top 25 most demanding fanbases in British football right now

After an excellent first six months in West London, Burrell, not long after finding the back of the net against Sheffield Wednesday in January 2026, was ruled out for over three months and didn't make his return until April. By that point, there was not much of the season to go, as QPR's play-off prospects faded in his absence.

This season, Burrell has remained an almost ever-present in the R's lineup, but with just two goals in eight league appearances thus far, both coming at home against Cardiff City in a 2-1 victory, he hasn't quite hit the heights hoped for him.

Now, Burrell has been absent since the last international break in mid-September after suffering an injury on international duty with Jamaica, and upon his return to fitness, will need to work his way back into the fold, especially with Richard Kone looking to have found his shooting boots.

Time is more on Burrell's side to justify exactly why Premier League interest ever emerged in the first place, as it wasn't too long ago that Football League World's QPR fan pundit, Louis Moir, made an eight-figure claim on the Jamaican.

"I do think it’s a bit too early in his career to talk about Premier League football, Burrell,” Moir told Football League World.

"He’s not had a full season with us in the Championship, and I’d be shocked if he was to leave.

"Of course, clubs are going to be interested in loads of players, but whether they actually make a move or put in the money that would probably make us willing to accept, you’re going to be talking £10 million or so, around that price range for a player who has impressed.

"[He was] unfortunate to get injured, but if it wasn’t for getting injured, who knows how many goals he’d be on? He’s had a cracking first season with us in the Championship.

"If he does well with us again next season, there could be even more interest, but I’d be baffled really if he was to go to the Premier League so soon in his career.

"I just can’t see it at all; it would take a lot of money, around £10 million or so."

Despite Burrell not quite having the electric start to the season as QPR supporters would have hoped, his value won't have decreased too much, and the R's will surely remain firm in their stance on the forward.

Whether he is worth an eight-figure fee at this stage remains to be seen, though what is certain is that he must start finding the back of the net with more consistency upon his return to the side to strengthen that claim, as both Sunderland and Wolves may feel as though they have dodged a bullet with this one.

How much do you think Burrell is worth right now? Have Sunderland and Wolves dodged a bullet in avoiding Burrell's addition? Share your thoughts below!

QPR look like real play-off contenders again, and having shown signs of challenging for the top six last time around, Stephan's side fell just short in his first year at the club.

This campaign, the former Strasbourg and Stade Rennes boss will have no intention of making any such mistake again, and will be imploring Burrell to hit some form sooner rather than later to maintain their play-off push.

It could be a historic year for QPR, and Burrell could be a crucial factor in it.

#2127. QPR and Bradford City won’t be shocked by Jack Wilshere, Luton Town situation

Luton Town have turned around their recent form after making a slower start to the new League One campaign compared to their rivals.

The Hatters went into the new season targeting a top two finish, with their sights set on returning to the Championship.

And they have worked their way back up to fourth in the standings after the opening 14 games of the term, winning seven and drawing three.

This has left Jack Wilshere’s side five points behind leaders Huddersfield Town, and only two adrift of second place Stockport County.

One aspect of the new campaign that hasn’t quite worked out for Luton is the arrival of Harrison Ashby from Newcastle United.

The full-back joined on loan from the Magpies, and has so far featured in eight of their 14 league games this season, including making three starts.

The 24-year-old hasn’t made much of an impact for the Hatters, and is struggling to break into Wilshere’s starting lineup on a consistent basis.

He played the full 90 minutes of the 2-0 win against Forest Green Rovers in the FA Cup last weekend, but that was his first time in the starting XI since 19 September, where he played against his former side Bradford City in a 1-0 loss.

Ashby previously spent the second half of last season on loan with the Bantams, where he played just eight times for Graham Alexander’s side in the league.

The defender struggled to prove his worth for the Yorkshire outfit, who were hoping his arrival could bolster their promotion hopes.

Can Harrison Ashby turn around his Luton Town stint? Comment your opinion below

Yet he didn’t even feature in the play-offs, as they lost to Bolton Wanderers in the semi-finals.

And his previous loan stint prior to moving to Valley Parade was also quite underwhelming for QPR, where he was unable to show he could compete at a Championship level.

Ashby is behind Isaiah Jones in the pecking order under Wilshere, and it’s difficult to see that changing in the immediate future.

But he has also fallen behind Hakeem Odoffin as well, even though the midfielder is not naturally a full-back.

Rob Edwards has opened up on Luton Town's single Premier League season

The 28-year-old has found himself moved into that position while Ashby was out with a groin injury, even playing there with Jones moved into a more advanced role as a winger.

Wilshere has found this solution, and this may leave Ashby out in the cold, unless he can find a way to convince the manager that he deserves a place in the team now that he is back fully fit.

If Ashby is unable to earn his way back into the Luton team between now and the January transfer window opening, then Newcastle may have to act.

The 24-year-old doesn’t look capable of being able to reach the level needed to become a part of their plans in the Premier League, even with their disappointing start to the new season.

#2126. 'Winning at the Emirates is very hard... but we were a team of warriors': Hull City hero GEOVANNI on his iconic goal against Arsenal, why it very nearly never happened and why the Tigers 'will always be in my heart'

Published: 21:00 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 06:07 EST, 7 November 2026

The greatest moment in Hull City's Premier League history began with Geovanni trying to go home.

'I was ill all night, I barely slept at all,' says Geovanni, who was gripped by a fever and thumping headache less than 24 hours before he was due to walk out at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium in September 2008. The Brazilian rang his wife from the team hotel to tell her he was coming home and planned to have someone pick him up.

Thankfully, his wife Roberta would not hear of it.

'God really used her that day,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'She said: "Geovanni, stay there, God will honour you. Hang on and tomorrow try to get a bit of sleep."'

When Hull staff came to his room the next morning, he asked to be left to sleep. He dosed up on medicine and went for lunch, but sat out the light pre-match training session with his temperature touching 38 degrees Celsius.

'And then I got to that game, which was so spectacular,' he says, 'and I was able to score and help Hull beat Arsenal.'

Geovanni unleashes a spectacular equaliser for Hull at the Emirates Stadium back in September 2008

The goal inspired a famous comeback win for the Tigers, who became only the second team to win away at Arsenal

It was Hull's first league meeting with Arsenal for 93 years, in the first top-flight season of the club's then 104-year history.

Arsene Wenger's side had started the day top of the table and Paul McShane's own goal put Arsenal ahead after 51 minutes. Most expected the floodgates to open.

But 11 minutes later up stepped Hull's brilliant Brazilian, a marquee signing from Manchester City in the summer of 2008 after the Tigers' unexpected promotion.

Geovanni cut inside Theo Walcott and sent a 25-yard rocket into Manuel Almunia's top corner. Daniel Cousin headed in a historic winner four minutes later and Hull became only the second side to beat Arsenal at the Emirates.

'Beating Arsenal at the Emirates is very hard, and we pulled it off,' says Geovanni, now 46, speaking from his home in Brazil. 'That was a team of warriors, great players, and we had a really good friendship. And that day we walked away with a great win.'

On Saturday, Hull return to the Emirates to face the champions and league leaders. The Tigers are 11th after nine games. It is a strong start that few predicted.

'Hull have to give 100 per cent, the maximum, be switched on the whole time,' says Geovanni. 'It's difficult, but it's not impossible, because Hull really did beat Arsenal.'

Eight days after the Emirates match, Geovanni did it again. A stunning 30-yard free-kick at White Hart Lane nestled into the top corner past his friend and compatriot Heurelho Gomes.

'We beat Tottenham with Gareth Bale, Luka Modric, all those players,' he says. 'For me, those two are top-drawer. They're two great players who left a mark on me.'

The win moved Hull into third and by the end of October they were level on points at the top. 'London 0 Hull 2' read the headline in the local paper, in reference to Hull band The Housemartins' 1986 album London 0 Hull 4, as the city revelled in its newfound fame.

Geovanni (centre) was part of another iconic Premier League moment, when Phil Brown gave his team a public dressing down at half-time of a loss at Manchester City

The Brazilian returned to Hull's MKM Stadium last year and received a hero's welcome

Geovanni took centre stage. Arriving on a free that summer after being released by Manchester City, he credits manager Phil Brown and assistant Brian Horton for giving him a second chance in the Premier League.

'They were very special people in allowing me to stay in England, which was my dream,' he says. 'And I learned a lot from both of them. Brian was a very experienced coach, he played for Hull, he managed there, so the affection and respect are huge. Whenever I can talk about them, I do.

'In the first year, Hull surprised a lot of people precisely because of the way we played. Sometimes we'd start in a 4-3-1-2, I played as the No10 behind two strikers. And if we were struggling to mark, I'd drop in to close down the left flank and we'd go back to a 4-4-2.'

The dressing room did the rest. Richard Garcia, an Australian winger with Uruguayan parents, helped translate team talks from English into Spanish and captain Ian Ashbee, Nicky Barmby and Bernard Mendy all made Geovanni feel welcome. 'I'm really happy about the friendships I made in that dressing room,' he says.

Geovanni was part of another of the Premier League's most iconic moments, when he and his team-mates received a public dressing down from his manager on the pitch at half-time of a 5-1 loss to Manchester City on Boxing Day 2008. Eleven months later, Jimmy Bullard scored a penalty before recreating the telling off in celebration.

'It was good for breaking the ice,' says Geovanni. 'From that day on the atmosphere got better too, because we can all make mistakes. The most important thing is to admit the mistake and move on.'

Geovanni's finest moment for Manchester City, with whom he spent one season after stints with Barcelona, Benfica and Cruzeiro, came in the Manchester derby, where he was called into the side by manager Sven-Goran Eriksson because Stephen Ireland was ill.

'He called me over and said, "Geovanni, this game... are you ready?". That was the best news I'd had all day, knowing I was going to start.' The day did, in fact, get better. Geovanni scored the only goal in a 1-0 victory.

Geovanni smashes home a winner for City in the Manchester derby, a year before his move to Hull

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages

He struck again against United in November 2008, in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages, while he also scored in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford in 2008.

'A player has to turn up in the big games,' he says. 'United were a machine back then: Giggs, Paul Scholes, Gary Neville, Anderson, Ronaldo, Rooney.'

Geovanni's greatest regret, though, remains that he didn't heed the advice of Barca boss Louis van Gaal, who wanted to turn the wannabe striker into a wing-back.

He reflects: 'If I could go back in time, I'd listen to what Van Gaal said, because it would have been easier for me to fight for a place at wing-back than as a striker, where there were great players: Javier Saviola, Rivaldo, Patrick Kluivert, Marc Overmars.'

Luiz Felipe Scolari, his coach at Cruzeiro, gave him his only senior Brazil cap, against Mexico at the 2001 Copa America. 'It was a dream for me: to leave a town of 4,000 people (Acaiaca) and one day represent Brazil,' he says. 'He (Scolari) was a father to me.'

These days Geovanni is a volunteer pastor in Belo Horizonte and runs a players' agency with his father-in-law and an old youth-team friend.

But Hull will always be in his heart. He has a picture of himself in a Hull shirt in his house and received a hero's return after heading back to the city last year.

'I love them (the fans). I have a very special affection for the Hull supporters,' he says. 'It was two years in which I gave everything. I went back there last year and was really well received, it was great: friends from my time there, the fans too.

Battling Blackburn's Damien Duff in a pre-season friendly in his Barcelona days. He spent only two seasons with the Catalan club, having left Cruzeiro to move to Europe

'I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart'

'And I know I left my mark on the club's history. Whenever people talk about Hull City, about Brazilians, they'll remember Geovanni, the time I spent there, the feats we achieved together.

'And I believe I gave those fans a lot of joy, in games that seemed impossible. God blessed me and I was able to score goals and bring joy to that city. I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart.

'My two years at Hull were perhaps the two most special years for me. The sweetest spell of my career.'

#2125. Don Goodman names the 3 EFL clubs that have shocked him the most so far

From unprecedented promotion pushes to shock relegations and unexpected free-scoring campaigns to the harshest of managerial sackings, the EFL prides itself on providing innumerable surprises, curveballs and twists and turns each campaign.

The 2026/27 term still remains in a relative infancy but has not fallen short of meeting such standards of saga, drama and surprise heading into the November international break, with various plot twists and odds-upsetting developments continuing to take centre-stage across the EFL sphere.

Whether it's the Championship, League One or League Two, the EFL simply never disappoints when it comes to conjuring up drama and shock, and the excitement among supporters is often fuelled by the unnerving - yet just as thrilling - reality that you really don't know what to expect outside of the Premier League.

But which clubs have produced the most significant surprises so far in 2026/27? EFL expert Don Goodman has offered his take...

One of the most recognisable faces and voices throughout the EFL landscape, Goodman scored freely for the likes of West Bromwich Albion, Wolves and Sunderland before entering the media after hanging up his boots and is now at the forefront of Football League proceedings as a pundit for Sky Sports.

Goodman is well-acquainted with the EFL's pulsating drama and unpredictability, then, and he has named the 3 clubs throughout all three divisions to have left him with the most surprises in the opening quarters of the current campaign.

The pundit initially raised Burnley's struggles towards the foot of the Championship table in the wake of from the Premier League in May before paying particular attention to Bromley's controversial and widely-condemned sacking of Andy Woodman after rising from the fifth-tier to a first-ever EFL promotion and then up to League One as champions last term during the 55-year-old's legendary reign.

Goodman has been surprised by Salford City, too, with the Ammies having soared to League Two's summit playing a swashbuckling brand of attack-minded football under ex-Malaysia boss Peter Cklamovski following defeat in last term's play-off final against Notts County.

Speaking to Football League World via Betway, Goodman explained: "We'll start with the bad which is obviously Burnley.

"Conceding 31 goals in 15 league games is poor, especially when two seasons ago in the Championship, in the whole season they conceded 16.

"I know that there's different personnel, but that is how far off it they are to being a top team in the Championship, so Burnley have shocked me how poor they’ve been.

"I think Bromley have shocked me by sacking Andy Woodman, who's brought them from the National League into League One.

"I am really shocked that they didn't have faith and a bit of patience with him having done what he's done for that football club. I think that's a shocker from Bromley and their hierarchy."

Football League World assesses and ranks the FIFTEEN best away fanbases in the EFL right now

His surprises weren't limited to the negatives, though, as Goodman then talked up Salford's early-season promotion ascent.

It may not surprise others as much considering the Greater Manchester outfit's run to Wembley at the end of the previous campaign before acquiring top-grade League Two talent in the form of Macaulay Langstaff and Luke Molyneux from Millwall and Doncaster Rovers respectively over the summer, of course, but the manner in which Cklamovksi's side have hit their rhythm has still left Goodman shocked for all the right reasons.

"I think a positive one is Salford City," he continued.

"After losing the first three games of the season, for them to win 10 and draw one of the last 11, winning eight in a row, they look unstoppable under Peter Cklamovski.

"The football that they're playing doesn't belong in League Two. It's brilliant to watch. They're far and away the best team, and I'm a little bit surprised by that in a good way."

Bromley's shock aforementioned dismissal of Woodman is certainly a worthy discussion point, and we're unlikely to see a harsher sacking in any of the three divisions all season despite the proclivity for brutally trigger-happy sackings within many EFL boardrooms.

The plucky Ravens had never previously competed above the fifth-tier in what had been a 132-year history before winning the National League play-offs under Woodman in 2024.

A respectable eleventh-placed finish left some surprised, but the real shock was in store last time out when Bromley saw off the likes of Cambridge United, Salford and Paul Warne's star-studded MK Dons side to lift the League Two title against all odds.

The South Londonders had struggled to find their feet at League One level, it must be said, though that was actually following the script of expectation after completely overhauling the squad which had spearheaded the club's shock upwards direction of travel in the first place.

What wasn't in the script, of course, was for Woodman - the most successful manager in Bromley's history after ascending to unimaginable peaks - to be relieved of his duties merely 10 games into the campaign in a meeting that, according to the man himself, lasted just four minutes.

Bromley, who were positioned in 23rd at the time following two wins from 10 but have lost three of their last four encounters across all competitions since parting company with Woodman, left the now-ex Ravens boss feeling "disappointed, upset and misled" by a brutal decision that undermined all his unprecedented achievements and has been slammed by the broader EFL community.

Woodman did, however, issue a telling reminder that the game's inability to follow expectation means that it never truly surprises us - and he may just be onto something there, after all.

Burnley's positioning inside the Championship relegation zone just months after dropping out of the Premier League and with a managerial casualty already on the list means that few clubs have surprised the masses more than the Clarets, and Woodman's departure from Bromley may not be topped in terms of sheer shock and harshness, yet plenty of other EFL clubs have also upset the odds for either the right or wrong reasons.

Level on points with the Clarets in the second-tier's bottom-three is Derby County, who were widely expected to plot a successful march into the expanded play-offs after finishing in eighth and just four points shy of sixth-placed Wembley winners Hull City but have instead endured a bitterly-disappointing campaign to prompt mass backlash towards under-fire manager John Eustace.

Higher up the Championship, however, both Stoke City and Swansea are bidding to defy the odds with somewhat-unexpected promotion pushes following mid-table finishes, with the latter representing fair value to compete for a top-two finish at this moment in time.

As for the League One promotion race, it's pretty much as you would expect, although Aaron Ramsey's under-embargo Oxford United side are earning plaudits in third position and find themselves ahead of larger, more free-spending clubs without their current transfer restrictions. Neil Harris' eighth-placed Cambridge, fresh off the back of promotion behind Bromley, also deserve some flowers.

What do you make of Don Goodman's selections? Who are the EFL clubs to have surprised you the most? Has your own club shocked you so far this season? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

Then in League Two, the real surprise position may just be Cheltenham Town's in fifth after winding up in 15th and 18th over the previous two campaigns.

Rotherham United, meanwhile, are facing the threat of successive relegations, which may offer some surprise in light of the Millers' previous status as a yo-yo outfit between the second and third-tiers, although the broader deep-seated issues at the ASSEAL New York Stadium provide more context behind a sudden nosedive.

More surprises, mind you, are only in store as the season toils on, and whereas the ecstasy and enjoyment for some will be rivalled by disappointment and frustration for others, the EFL is only promising to retain its peerless aversion to predictability.

#2124. West Brom told to ‘find the money’ and sign Blackburn Rovers star

EFL pundit Tom Garratt has urged West Brom to ‘find the money’ to sign Blackburn Rovers ace Andri Gudjohnsen during the January transfer window.

Speaking on the latest edition of the Pyramid Podcast, Garratt, hosting alongside Callum Fowler, believes Gudjohnsen could be the missing piece in the Albion jigsaw to help the Black Country outfit seal promotion back to the Premier League.

James Morrison’s men continue to be in the promotion conversation, heading into the latest international break unbeaten in their last six games and securing four victories in that period.

Their latest 3-0 romping of Millwall last weekend leaves Albion fifth in the second-tier standings, sitting just one point off the summit in such a compact top eight.

Much was made at the beginning of the season about West Brom’s lack of a clinical frontman, with it one of the main concerns as to why some connected with Albion feel a promotion push may fade away in time.

Controlling shareholder Shilen Patel may be able to fix the issue in the January transfer window, should funds become available, and it could well be the difference maker in whether they return to the big time or not.

So, with this in mind, well-known EFL pundit and West Brom supporter Tom Garratt has demanded the club make a deal to sign one of the best-performing strikers in the Championship, at this moment in time.

Despite having such an excellent summer transfer window, one criticism from some West Brom supporters at the club was not going all out to recruit a striker who could score regularly at Championship level.

Albion were reportedly interested in Southampton’s Cameron Archer, but missed out on a deal due to his high wages on the South Coast, with the 24-year-old eventually going on to move to French outfit Auxerre instead, where he has scored six goals in eight Ligue 1 games.

The Baggies were busy during the summer window revamping some of the forward line, replacing the outgoings of Josh Maja and Daryl Dike with Barney Stewart and Jimmy-Jay Morgan.

Morgan in particular has been a roaring success so far, grabbing eight goal contributions in 15 league matches so far for the club, but is not a conventional centre-forward, favouring drifting over to the left-hand side while a proper number nine stays central.

Stewart, since moving from Scottish side Falkirk, has found opportunities hard to come by and has netted just once for his new club so far, while Aune Heggebo in his second season at the club has also found himself in and out of the side, with most of his success coming off the bench and making an impact in recent times.

Thankfully, much of Albion’s early success has been down to players in other positions chipping in with goals, with the likes of Isaac Price notching six times and providing three assists, while fellow summer arrival Felix Horn Myhre now has three goals to his name in the blue and white stripes.

West Bromwich Albion signed Felix Horn Myhre for just £3.1 million in the summer ahead of Spanish outfit Elche

Despite that, Albion fans would be put at ease to see a clinical frontman lead the line from January onwards, with a regular source of goals badly needed for the Baggies to continue to fight towards the top end of the division.

Speaking on the latest episode of the Pyramid Podcast with Callum Fowler, EFL pundit Tom Garratt has demanded West Brom ‘find the money’ to sign Blackburn Rovers star Andri Gudjohnsen in January.

Gudjohnsen is already into double figures for goals from his opening 14 league games this season, notably scoring a brace at The Hawthorns against West Brom last month, while also netting in Rovers' 2-1 victory over West Ham last weekend.

And Garratt was gushing about the 24-year-old's strike against the Hammers, believing he is the second-best striker in the division and can help the Baggies turn their promotion hopes into a reality.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

Garratt said: “This is a plea to West Bromwich Albion again.

“Find the money, find the money somewhere, it’s there somewhere. (Tom) Fellows went for a lot of money. We have sold players in recent years, go and buy (Andri) Gudjohnsen.

“His movement for the goal is so, so good. Don’t get me wrong, it’s a ‘tap in’, but his movement to get there is unbelievable. He is the second-best striker in this league.”

There’s no doubt that what’s missing most in West Brom’s squad is the addition of a striker that can usually net between 20 and 25 goals in a full Championship season, with Albion continuing to bank on the likes of Isaac Price to perform and find the back of the net consistently.

But over time, that’s at risk of drying up, so Albion must do all they can at the turn of the new year to bring in a forward who has an eye for goal and can make a real difference at the top end of the pitch.

And while it’s likely to be one of the areas the Baggies hierarchy look to address, the chances of Blackburn’s Andri Gudjohnsen signing on the dotted line at The Hawthorns is bound to be extremely low.

West Brom fans, could you see the Baggies moving for Andri Gudjohnsen in January, or do you feel he's an unrealistic target? Drop your thoughts in the comments below!

After having much of a revamp during the summer transfer window, Albion are likely to not possess many financial funds in January, with clubs across the country much more active in the loan market as bigger sides to themselves decide to temporarily part ways with players who can’t break into their first-team crop.

Meanwhile, Gudjohnsen’s impact at Blackburn cannot be understated. His 10 goals so far have been a massive reason as to why Rovers sit on the periphery of the top eight, and while the Lancashire outfit have let go of some stars on the cheap in recent times, there’s no reason to suggest why Blackburn wouldn’t want a massive fee to part them from their Icelandic star - a price that only Premier League level sides can afford.

You do feel if Gudjohnsen was to move on from Ewood Park in January, then it would be permanently, so factoring in what would be such a high price to secure his services and an unwillingness to let him leave on loan, in particular to a Championship rival, you would think it’s a very low chance that West Brom will be Gudjohnsen’s next club.

However, there’s no reason why Albion shouldn’t be able to land a similar goalscoring forward on loan in January, with the winter window always throwing up such unexpected deals the closer the clock ticks towards the deadline.

#2123. Michael Carrick reacts to Man Utd boos after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick admitted Manchester United’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur was a painful result, after his side failed to protect the lead against 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford.

Manchester United looked set to claim three points when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the second half off Cunha’s low cross, but Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser in injury time left Carrick facing more questions on United’s performance and his future.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, the United manager felt his players improved after the break but failed to handle the situation when victory was within reach.

“It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time,” Carrick said.

“But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position – we should see it through. We have to manage those situations.”

United have now conceded two late goals that have cost them valuable points, something Carrick believes has made their position look worse than it might have otherwise.

Asked whether a lack of confidence had contributed to United’s slow start, he disagreed but admitted matches can quickly slip away from his side.

The boos at half-time and full-time also clearly affected him.

“It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”

#2122. Bryan Mbeumo reacts to Man Utd draw with Tottenham

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Bryan Mbeumo admitted Manchester United have work to do after their frustrating 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, despite scoring a superb second-half goal at Old Trafford.

The Cameroon international put Manchester United ahead in the 73rd minute, finishing in the far corner after Matheus Cunha created the opportunity from a low cross. However, Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory, even though Tottenham had been reduced to 10 men following Rodrigo Bentancur’s red card.

Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2).

3 – Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? pic.twitter.com/DuSpvymZfu

Speaking to Sky Sports after the game, Mbeumo acknowledged that United had taken too long to find their rhythm.

“We took time to get into the game, but we played well in the second half. In the first half, that wasn’t us, we had to change. We tried to get at them,” he said.

Mbeumo recognised the threat Tottenham posed and admitted the result was disappointing, particularly given United’s position in the game before Solanke’s late goal.

“We know Spurs have good players who can be dangerous. It’s a bit disappointing, we need to work on things.”

United have struggled for consistency in the opening weeks of the season, and dropping points after taking the lead will do little to ease the pressure on Carrick. Mbeumo, however, insisted the team must look ahead rather than dwell on the setback.

“We need to keep going forward, as we have a lot of games.”

Michael Carrick was pleased with Mbeumo’s contribution, highlighting both the quality of his finish and the different roles he has played since joining United.

“Bryan’s done great. It was a fantastic finish again; he’s obviously played different roles for us but we know what he offers,” the United manager said.

“He’s got good quality and obviously the more goals he scores, the better. He’s doing really well for us.”

Mbeumo’s goal was one of the few bright moments in another difficult afternoon for United. Carrick’s team must now find a way to turn things around from here after just six points from six games.

#2121. 'I want to win the Ballon d'Or': JJ Gabriel sets out his lofty ambitions as Man United wonderkid, 16, closes in on move to Real Madrid after quitting Red Devils

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 06:08 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 06:09 EST, 7 November 2026

Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel has revealed his ambition to win the Ballon d'Or as he dropped the clearest hint yet that he is heading to Real Madrid in an interview with Spanish media.

The 16-year-old sensation stunned Manchester United with a formal transfer request in September and is now on the verge of finalising his move to the Spanish capital.

Daily Mail Sport exclusively revealed Madrid's growing confidence in securing the free-scoring starlet last month, with Gabriel now having secured a European Union passport through his mother's Cypriot heritage.

The youngster, who is currently working with a personal trainer in Madrid, practically confirmed the transfer in an interview with Spanish newspaper Marca on Friday night, admitting he had a clear preference to Real over archrivals Barcelona.

'Obviously Madrid,' Gabriel told the outlet when asked which LaLiga giant he preferred.

According to the newspaper, who expects his move to be finalised in January, Gabriel's response prompted a laugh from his father and mentor Joe O'Cearuill.

Manchester United prodigy JJ Gabriel poses for his interview with Spanish newspaper Marca

Gabriel is set to complete a move to Real Madrid after formally requesting to leave Old Trafford

'My dream is to win the Ballon d'Or,' explained the talented youngster, who scored a hat-trick for Manchester United in the UEFA Youth League just days before submitting his transfer request.

Although Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona's Lamine Yamal narrowly missed out on winning the 2026 Ballon d'Or - which was held aloft by England captain and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane - the two LaLiga giants have long had a rich association with the award, regularly producing the world's best footballer.

While sources at United insist there has been no club-to-club contact, it appears only a matter of time before Gabriel is sporting Real Madrid's iconic all-white jersey.

It is understood Gabriel will play for Madrid's Castilla team, which plays in Spain's third division, as well as in the Youth League.

Gabriel broke a series of records playing for United youth teams, including becoming the youngest player to feature in the Under-18s.

The prodigy, who was 14 when he netted twice on his debut, has also played - and scored - for Manchester United's Under-21 side.

The Red Devils were rocked in September when Gabriel and his representatives made a bombshell request to have his academy contract torn up. That request was immediately refused by United and, while there was faint hope that a compromise could have been found to keep him at Old Trafford, he has stayed away ever since.

Gabriel's dream is to win the Ballon d'Or, which was awarded this year to England's Harry Kane

As Daily Mail Sport previously reported, United's decline since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson has been the driving force behind Gabriel's family seeking an exit. United have not won a Premier League title since 2013.

A source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

His father has been described as a fiercely ambitious, pushy parent and is credited with the decision to get JJ out of United in an attempt to fast-track his career.

#2120. Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp tear into Man Utd after Tottenham draw

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United have come under fresh criticism after their disappointing 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur, with Sky Sports pundits Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp questioning the team’s performance and the challenges facing Michael Carrick.

Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory at Old Trafford after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half. However, despite Tottenham being reduced to 10 men, Dominic Solanke’s late equaliser denied Carrick’s side all three points.

Gary Neville felt Tottenham deserved the points, pointing to Solanke’s late goal and his impact as Tottenham captain.

“Tottenham deserved a point. That was a really important moment for Solanke. He’d missed some big chances and was captain for the first time,” Neville said on Sky Sports.

“They were the better team by far. If they’d left without a point, it would have been terrible for them.”

The former United defender also expressed concern about what the result means for Carrick, who faces increasing pressure to improve performances and results.

“Michael Carrick is left with a lot to think about. It was a worrying day in terms of the level of performance and a big week ahead.”

Manchester United spent massively in the summer to overhaul their midfield. However, Jamie Redknapp was critical of the performance he saw on the pitch.

“I do not see enough connections in that midfield, and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back,” Redknapp said.

“Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is a theme this season.”

The former Liverpool midfielder also questioned United’s energy and attacking organization, suggesting the squad is not strong enough to meet the demands placed upon it.

“Their energy levels are not good enough, and they look loose going forward; there was no real structure.”

Redknapp added that Carrick cannot fix every issue alone, insisting the manager needs backing to improve the squad.

“The squad is not good or strong enough, and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect.”

#2119. English football’s top 25 biggest football clubs named and ranked by AI

A debate that will rage forever but one that remains fierce in English football is who is the biggest club in the land - and, between sets of supporters, whose club is bigger than the others.

The birthplace of the sport, football is perhaps the biggest cultural, political and emotional phenomenon in English society and wanting to be a fan of a club towards the top of its notional hierarchy does mean a lot to many.

Be it based on titles won, trophies gained, the amount of match-going supporters or even fans from overseas; the size of a club is not something decided empirically and therefore the debate will always rage on.

Subjective and controversial no matter how it is discussed or deciphered, there is a new form of trying to find a definitive answer in the modern world and that is with the use of AI - and so we have asked ChatGPT to rank the 25 biggest clubs in English football - whatever that really does mean.

Whether it be years spent in the top-flight, the size of a club’s fan base, their trophies won or historical significance; here is the list of the top 25 biggest clubs according on AI.

Squeezed into the 25 biggest clubs in England according to ChatGPT are Portsmouth, with their two league titles and historically excellent support the reasons outlined for being in the top 25.

Pompey, known for a raucous atmosphere at Fratton Park, entered into the Football League in 1920 and won successive titles shortly after the Second World War. The now Championship outfit fell out of the top four in 1959 and only experienced one further season before a seven-year stint on the Premier League during the 2000s - a period that saw them win the FA Cup, as well as reach another final, and play European football, too.

One of the oldest teams in the Football League or the EFL or, simply, English football and football altogether; next on AI’s list of the top 25 biggest clubs is Stoke City.

Established in 1863, Stoke have one major honour to their name with the 1972 League Cup, having been FA Cup runners-up to Manchester City in 2011. The Potters have spent large swathes of their history in the top-flight with their most recent stint lasting ten seasons between 2008 and 2018 before a frustrating malaise back down in the Championship, albeit challenging again this time around.

The first ever Football League champions marks Preston North End out as 23rd on AI’s list with the history and tradition of English football perhaps most well represented by Preston’s early dominance.

North End won the league and FA Cup double in the 1888-89 season as the original ‘invicibles’ without losing across the campaign before backing up their league title a season later. That history has had to count for a lot for PNE, though, having not been a top-flight club since the days of Sir Tom Finney; relegated in 1960-61 and yet to return as they now battle against relegation down to League One this season.

From the city of the oldest football club in the world, Sheffield FC, 22nd on ChatGPT’s list of the biggest club in England are four-time FA Cup winners Sheffield United.

The Blades, who also have a league title to their name winning the league in the 1897-98 campaign, are one of the more storied cup teams and one of the more historic, albeit not a founding member. They achieved promotion to the top-flight in 1894 and have remained there until 1934 before yo-yoing between the top two divisions until the 1980s. That yo-yoing has returned in the last decade or so with their last seven full seasons being split three in the top-flight and four in the second-tier.

Next up on the list chosen or suggested by AI is another Championship outfit and this time it is two-time English champion Burnley, who are struggling down at the bottom end of the second-tier now.

A founding member of the Football League, Burnley have spent much of the last decade and a bit in the Premier League, having not been in the top-flight from 1975-76 until one season in the 2009-10 campaign. The Clarets, who won the league in both 1921 and 1960, as well as an FA Cup in 1913, are one of few teams to have won the English title while also spending a fair bit of time in the fourth-tier.

Having touched upon several clubs with historic significance, next on the list is one of the modern day ‘bigger clubs’ with AI putting Leicester City 20th on the list.

Famously, The Foxes produced a ‘great escape’ before winning the 2015-16 Premier League title - becoming the first outsider of 5000/1 odds to ever win in any sport. The next half a decade saw them begin to cement themselves as top four challengers as well as then win the FA Cup but the last few years has not gone well and they now reside back in League One - and struggling to find the consistency to bounce back after back-to-back relegations.

A local rival of Leicester in the East Midlands and another team struggling this season is next on the list with two-time English champions and Football League founding member Derby County.

Raucous crowds at Pride Park have dampened this season with The Rams struggling down at the bottom end of the Championship table. Two-time league winners in the 1970s, Derby regularly knocked on the door of promotion during the 2010s but they have spent just one season in the Premier League, setting the record for the lowest points tally of 11, since the 2001-02 campaign.

Rated as the bigger of the Sheffield clubs by AI; next on the list at number 18 are United’s arch-rivals Sheffield Wednesday with their four league titles, three FA Cups and one League Cup.

The Owls are again one of the more storied teams in English football with dominance at both the start of the 1900s and in the late-1920s. Wednesday could perhaps be argued to be the biggest sleeping giant in English given football, given that they haven’t been in the top-flight since relegation in the 1999-00 campaign, having previously spent most of their history at that level. They are one of two clubs outside of the top two divisions to be in ChatGPT's list.

Perhaps surprisingly low down on the list considering their well acknowledged European Cup history; Nottingham Forest are rated the 17th biggest club in England according to AI.

ChatGPT suggests Nottingham Forest’s two triumphs in the European Cup are only enough for 17th. During the era of Brian Clough at the City Ground, Forest won a league title, four League Cups, the Community Shield, two European Cups and the Super Cup. Outside of that 18-year reign, though, Forest’s other major honours both came in the FA Cup in 1898 and 1959. Now back in the Premier League; it is where many believe the club should reside.

Next up on ChatGPT’s list of the 25 biggest clubs in England is a storied stalwart of the top two divisions in English football from the midlands, West Bromwich Albion.

Five-time FA Cup winners and founding members of the Football League, West Brom also have a league title under their belt, won in 1920. Albion have had some real highs as a part of English football’s furniture with their late 70s team of Laurie Cunningham, Brendan Baston, Cyrille Regis, Tony Brown, John Wile and Bryan Robson one that is fondly remembered by many a neutral. On only one occasion ever in their 148-year history have The Baggies not been playing in either the top-flight or the second-tier.
