#2015. West Ham will rue lack of sell – on clause as player’s value skyrockets

Sixteen players departed West Ham United last summer as the relegation exodus took its toll, along with the huge debt and cash flow issues that forced the Hammers to part with most of their more valuable assets.

£190 million raised from the sale of just four players certainly kept the accountants happy, whilst fans have had to deal with the anguish that comes from watching former favourites turn out for clubs who once were West Ham’s rivals.

One player in particular looks to be about to realise his stated ambition: Whilst he was still a Hammer, El Hadji Malick Diouf made no secret of his desire to play for a ‘top club’ one day – which didn’t exactly endear him to Irons supporters.

£35 million plus add-ons for Diouf seemed too good to turn down: Now there are claims he’s worth £20 million more

His transfer to Brentford bolstered the West Ham accounts by a cool £35 million but it seems west London is just the next rung on the ladder for the ambitious 21 year old.

Despite a dodgy start to his Brentford career, apparently Diouf’s left-footed curling crosses and pacy wing work is getting him noticed in all the right places. ‘Top clubs’, it seems, are indeed casting envious eyes over the left back’s CV, according to caughtoffside who claim the defender is now worth up to £55 million as “Chelsea and Liverpool make contact over €60m rated Diouf”.

I doubt anyone at Hammers HQ had the foresight to put a sell-on clause in his sale contract: West Ham fans will be incredulous, as was I, that the amiable left back with the booming crosses but dodgy defensive positioning has magically morphed into a £55 million rated player in a matter of months.

#2014. Newcastle United offer of £11million a year wages to Gregor Kobel reported by German media

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

It has now been reported in Germany that Newcastle United tried to buy Gregor Kobel in the summer.

SportBild claiming that United attempted to sign the Borussia Dortmund goalkeeper before then eventually signing Lukas Hornicek as the new NUFC number one.

Whether Newcastle United really did try to buy Gregor Kobel is an unknown.

They report that it was Gregor Kobel himself who said no to Newcastle United. Which again, may or may not be true.

However, you definitely tend to be thinking this is yet another fantasy transfer story when you hear what else SportBild are claiming as part of this summer transfer that didn’t happen.

They claim that Newcastle United offered Gregor Kobel a huge pay rise to come to Tyneside.

SportBild stating that Newcastle United offered €13m (approx £11m) a year, which is around €250,000 (£210,000 a week).

That is simply ridiculous, for anybody to believe that.

As well as all the other financial restrictions that prevent Newcastle United offering the same wages (and transfer fees) as the ‘Premier League Big Six’ and certain other clubs overseas, United faced a summer that was seriously impacted by UEFA SCR impact.

This meant Newcastle United had to sell key players for large fees and get high wage earners off the books, in order to rebuild the squad by recruiting lower wage younger players from overseas.

Bruno Guimaraes was the highest earner at Newcastle United on around £8m per year (£160,000 a week).

The idea that NUFC were selling the likes of Bruno, Tonali and Gordon, only to then offer a new goalkeeper millions more than any of them were receiving in wages, is beyond laughable.

#2013. New Bromley boss Karl Robinson heaps praise on 'megastar' Jermain Defoe - with Premier League legend in talks over dugout return after walking out on Woking

Published: 08:00 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 13:33 EST, 7 November 2026

New Bromley boss Karl Robinson has hailed Premier League 'megastar' Jermain Defoe as the ultimate professional following his abrupt departure from Woking.

Daily Mail Sport revealed on Tuesday that Defoe is in talks to join Robinson's backroom staff at League One strugglers Bromley after Andy Woodman's dismissal last month.

And while his appointment has yet to be confirmed, Robinson jumped at the chance to wax lyrical about Defoe at his inauguration on Thursday.

Bromley sit bottom of League One but their new boss believes Defoe's meticulous attention to detail would help the players find another gear.

'There's been a lot of talk but there always is with names like Jermain Defoe, who is a megastar. He's one of the greatest Premier League strikers of all time,' Robinson said.

'I have to raise and change the narrative of what this stands for,' the new boss pointed to the Bromley badge on his jumper.

Jermain Defoe is in talks to join League One strugglers Bromley as Karl Robinson's assistant

Former Salford City manager Robinson has hailed 'megastar' Defoe as the ultimate professional

'I have to bring people in to make me the best version of myself. I spoke to people who know Jermain and played with him.

'He was always first in. All the players who have played with him will tell you that. Steven Gerrard will tell you that.

'He was first in and still in the training ground at 4pm - massages, recovery, gym, video analysis of the players he's playing against.

'I was speaking to him about something completely different the other day and we were talking about discipline and professionalism.

'I said to him: "what do you do that for?". He went: "If I do everything right Monday to Friday and I play poorly, I can accept it because I've done everything in the week to be the best version of myself."

'I'm listening and I've got goose pimples on my arm. Then I'm thinking, that's probably why you're Jermain Defoe, because he did everything he possibly could to maximise his talent.

Defoe has been out of work since walking away from National League side Woking after just four months at the helm amid a strained relationship with the club's director of football.

The 44-year-old took charge of the final six games of last season and was expected to lead the club into the new campaign.

However, he failed to report for work on the eve of the season before contacting the club later that day to inform them he would not be returning.

The former England international and Tottenham Hotspur striker would add top-level experience to the dressing room, having scored 163 Premier League goals in 496 appearances - ranking 10th on the Premier League's scoring charts.

Robinson spoke as though he idolised Defoe when quizzed on his potential appointment, highlighting his humility and relentlessness as key assets to succeed as a coach.

'Failure isn't falling short, it's when you don't maximise your talent. And I think some of the players here haven't maximised their athletic, technical and tactical capabilities', Robinson added.

'For whatever reason, we need to find the key to what that is. I think someone like Jermain (would bring that) because he maximised everything he was and everything he is.

'That's almost the secret behind the genius of the top players. It's their attention to detail, professionalism and discipline – he does that over and over again.

'He's tried to manage in non-league as well. That, in itself, is dropping your ego to learn.'

Although Bromley are still working on finalising Defoe's appointment, he is expected to join Robinson in the dugout at Hayes Lane. The Ravens host Rotherham in the first round of the FA Cup this weekend as Robinson takes his first game in charge.

#2012. West Ham Defender’s Remarkable Numbers Reveal January Transfer Problem

A recent X post by Luke, better known as LouOrns, showed some Championship centre-back analysis revealing that despite our shaky defence, Konstantinos Mavropanos is doing things that almost nobody else in the division can.

Looking at defenders with over 700 minutes played, the data shows a league dominated by specialists. Some centre-backs win everything in the air but struggle to contribute in possession. Others are comfortable progressing the ball but lack the physical dominance required to thrive in the Championship. Mavropanos is a rare exception. Winning more than 83% of his aerial duels while also posting progressive passing numbers comfortably above the league average, the Greek international combines two qualities that are rarely found in the same player. Only Portsmouth’s Regan Poole comes close to matching that balance, underlining just how unique Mavropanos’ profile has become.

What makes Mavropanos particularly impressive is that he is far more than a defender who simply attacks long balls. His progressive passing numbers are comfortably above the Championship average.

While defenders such as Billy Koumetio (Charlton), Ben Cabango (Swansea) and Nasser Djiga (Wolves) provide a respectable balance, none can match the Greek’s combination of aerial superiority and distribution.

That balance is precisely what makes him such a valuable asset. In a division built on physical battles, second balls and direct football, having a centre-back who consistently wins first contact whilst also driving possession forward provides a clear competitive edge, though it needs another three defenders and a goalkeeper to follow suit!

Dinos has posted some seriously impressive numbers

The chart paints a simple picture: many defenders excel at one aspect of the game. Very few excel at both.

And the data still doesn’t tell the full story.

What the chart does not show is goals. Mavropanos has already contributed five goals this season, an outstanding return for a central defender and further evidence of his all-round impact.

The Greek colossus is one of the rare exceptions to the rule, a centre-back performing at the very highest Championship standard.

West Ham are expected to receive January bids, and with a season drifting towards mid-table obscurity, may struggle to persuade our one and only key defender to remain at the London Stadium.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

#2011. Bayern won’t sign Rio Ngumoha after missing their chance in the summer – opinion

Bayern Munich are reportedly confident that there is a deal to be done with Liverpool for talented youngster Rio Ngumoha.

The Reds were understood to be the subject of some probing from the Bavarian giants, with discussions said to have taken place with the winger’s brother.

Whether Liverpool feel the same way… well, let’s just be clear on this: they don’t.

As Mick Brown noted in his latest report with Football Insider: “From what I hear, Bayern Munich are pretty confident there is a deal to be done.

“When there’s all this talk about making contact with his agents, speaking to the player, what it might cost, that stuff doesn’t happen unless they think they can do a deal.

“Whether Liverpool feel the same way, I have my doubts, because he has such obvious potential and Andoni Iraola has been pretty clear he is part of his plans.

“I don’t think he’s the finished article, but not many players are at 18, there are still areas of his game where he has to improve, so maybe that’s where the speculation comes from.”

Mick goes on to note that the Reds are currently giving Ngumoha everything he could realistically hope for at an elite European outfit. There is a pathway to the senior team and he’s already picked up 642 minutes (Transfermarkt) of action in the famous red shirt this season.

On top of that, his all-round game is being carefully developed, with appearances roughly split between both flanks.

And most importantly? Liverpool aren’t burning the player out — Andoni Iraola is managing the teenager’s minutes, rotating alongside Bradley Barcola, Victor Munoz and Cody Gakpo.

So, Bayern may feel a deal can be done, but realistically, can they offer the 18-year-old substantially more than he’s already receiving at Liverpool?

It’s worth pointing out that, as is indeed the case across Europe’s biggest outfits, Bayern’s shortlist is far from limited to Liverpool’s No.73. Names like Antonio Nusa and Oskar Pietuszewski are also highly rated by the club, with the former thought to be well-admired by Bayern chief Max Eberl.

But the important distinction to make here is that Ngumoha will not come cheap – far from it, compared to the two names alone we’ve just listed. And if Bayern already valued the versatile winger at €70m [£58.3m] in the summer, can you imagine how much his value has skyrocketed since becoming an important part of Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool squad? We’re surely talking in the territory of at least upwards of £7om, at a conservative estimate.

#2009. West Ham Insider Reveals Recruitment Mess Behind Club’s Decline

West Ham United are still suffering because of years of bad recruitment, Claret & Hugh has been told by a Hammers insider today. The source, who did not wish to be named, described the situation as a mess and laid the blame for the club’s current predicament firmly and squarely at muddled, poor recruitment.

Speaking to Claret & Hugh, the source said:

“It’s all down to recruitment and it’s been bad, a real mess.”

“It’s a hodge podge with players being brought from everywhere by loads of different people. We’re years behind and needed a complete reset, we had to start again and consider how we recruit.”

Honest words, and not ones that many West Ham fans would disagree with. The club has spent years changing managers, recruitment chiefs and transfer strategies, seemingly without allowing any one approach enough time to work. The result is a squad assembled under several different regimes, with little evidence of a consistent long-term plan.

It has always been Daniel Křetínský’s wish at West Ham to have a director of football in charge, and whilst we don’t have that exact job title at the club currently, Nils Koppen, as Director of Player Recruitment, is as good as a director of football in all but name.

What is clear is that the club are going to have to rebuild the recruitment structure brick by brick. And it’s worth pointing out that even as recently as the summer, there was still something of a mix-up, with a blend of recruitment ideas and Nuno Espírito Santo being allowed to bring in three players in Joël Piroe, Manor Solomon and Morato.

Kretinsky is a big believer in the structured recruitment model

That is hardly the definition of a joined-up recruitment strategy, although it’s also important to recognise that Koppen arrived with very little time to prepare for the summer window. The bigger issue is whether West Ham are finally prepared to commit to a consistent approach rather than changing direction whenever the manager changes.

We’re semi-lucky in one respect because we do have another transfer window coming up in January, giving Koppen and Scott Parker an opportunity to address some of the more obvious problems within the squad.

But this is definitely a time when West Ham have to commit to a transfer policy and allow it to play out and bear fruit over a number of seasons. Toying with an approach and then giving up, as we did with both Tim Steidten and Kyle Macaulay, is precisely the sort of short-term thinking that has contributed to the problem.

The club cannot keep appointing recruitment specialists, allowing them to start rebuilding the squad and then abandoning the entire project when results turn sour. At some point, West Ham have to decide what sort of players they want, how they’re going to identify them and who is ultimately responsible for bringing them in.

January offers an opportunity to begin correcting some of the mistakes, but the problems described by our source won’t be fixed in a single transfer window. If West Ham are genuinely years behind in their recruitment, the rebuild needs to be given the time and consistency that previous attempts have lacked.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

Where’s all this money coming from to fund the (start of) this overhaul. I can’t recall all the figures now but debt in excess of £200m, some of which had to (and has been) repaid, losing £100m a year and whilst wages have reduced by, say 50%, so has revenue. Unless Kretinsky is now a 45% and the major shareholder ( there appears to be conflicting info as to whether this transaction has completed) he is, based on history, little chance of him providing a transfer kitty and even if he is how does ‘FFP’ come into the equation?

I don’t think we needed a club insider to tell us about this issue. Yes not all signings will work out, but our success rate has been particularly poor in the last 3 years. I am not against a manager making suggestions as you allude to with Nuno, but they must be agreed by all relevant parties, then it becomes a cooperative relationship between manager and DOF.

The issue is that poor recruitment rarely costs directly on the books. Players amortise and those that don’t work out at all go out on loan bringing in loan fees.

The real problem lies in the contributions that they do not make. We invest and don’t lose out on the books but we do lose out in having invested in a player who did not contribute for us.

That affects results so affects success so affects us financially in that respect. Repeated poor investments.

It seems a shame that Daniel Kretinsky was not exerting influence at the time when David Moyes was also trying to build a consistent team.

We had it all then. We needed to continue with the Jarrod Bowen type of recruitment. We needed to back the manager and his coaching staff.

Instead, we were treated to exotic ideas of radical change which turned out to be a waste of money, time and a football club.

Tim Steidten could not believe his luck and bank balance as he scoured the world for excuses to spend on as high a profile as possible players to add to and become the basis of his team. No thoughts as to how these players would work in the game plans with the other players we already had. Only a passing reference to the team coach as the stars were aligned. The manager’s fault when success on the field was not forthcoming.

Poor recruitment played its part but continuity and investment in building upon a solid foundation was the real problem.

Let us hope that Scott Parker is allowed to continue to build our new team and not just until a more exotic name like Pellegrini or Lopetegui gets whispered into the ears of Daniel Kretinsky.

We have an opportunity now. We must take it.

#2007. West Ham Linked With Argentine Goalkeeper As Parker Plans January

West Ham United have been linked with a move for River Plate goalkeeper Santiago Beltrán, with Argentine publication TyC Sports reporting that the Hammers are among the clubs monitoring the youngster. Atlético Madrid are also named as interested parties, although there is no suggestion that West Ham have made an offer or opened negotiations.

River Plate are reportedly prepared to discuss a departure if an offer of US$15 million or more arrives, with the club already considering how they might replace their highly-rated goalkeeper. Beltrán has enjoyed an impressive breakthrough season, making 45 appearances and keeping 19 clean sheets, while also earning recognition from the Argentina national team.

The reported interest comes at an interesting time for West Ham, with Scott Parker facing an increasingly obvious problem between the posts. However, I would suggest the goalkeeper situation is only one of two major priorities for Nils Koppen when the January transfer window opens.

West Ham sold more than £200 million worth of players during the summer transfer window and spent just under £40 million on recruitment. Therefore, I would already hope that there is money set aside for January, rather than it becoming a straight choice between signing a goalkeeper or a striker.

Koppen wants to sign a goalkeeper in January

The problems in front of goal have been well documented, with Koppen already making enquiries about potential replacements for Taty Castellanos. But the goalkeeping situation is arguably just as concerning, as the numbers surrounding Mads Hermansen make increasingly uncomfortable reading.

Parker cannot realistically expect to mount a successful promotion challenge if he doesn’t have confidence in his goalkeeper and continues to struggle to find a reliable source of goals.

As for the reported US$15 million valuation of Beltrán, I’m not going to sit here and pretend I’ve watched the goalkeeper play. I haven’t, and I’m certainly not going to offer a technical assessment of somebody I haven’t properly studied.

But if he is the right man for the job, realistically West Ham cannot afford to hesitate over paying that sort of money.

The club has already spent far too long muddling its recruitment strategy, and the appointment of Koppen should mean we finally have somebody identifying players who fit a longer-term plan. The recent focus on recruiting a new centre-forward is encouraging, but that cannot be allowed to become an excuse for ignoring the goalkeeping department.

I would like to think that the money generated by last summer’s sales gives West Ham sufficient financial flexibility to address both positions. This isn’t an either/or situation.

If Beltrán is genuinely the goalkeeper Koppen and Parker believe can improve West Ham, then make the investment. But don’t forget the striker, because we have problems at both ends of the pitch and neither is going to disappear by itself.

One transfer insider has talked up the probability of Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk signing a new contract at Anfield in the next few months.

The 35-year-old’s current deal with the Reds expires at the end of this season, and he seemed relaxed over his future when discussing the topic with reporters after the win over Crystal Palace on Sunday.

That update from the skipper comes just as Alisson Becker (whose contract is also due to expire in 2027) voiced his desire to remain on Merseyside beyond then, with the goalkeeper’s agent opening talks over a prospective extension.

Speaking on The TEAMtalk podcast, Graeme Bailey claimed that Van Dijk has a strong chance of securing a new contract at Liverpool due to the positive impact that his performances have had on young centre-back partner Jeremy Jacquet.

The reporter said of the Dutchman: “Obviously he’s out of contract in the summer. He’s gonna be another year older as well. He signed a huge contract back in 2025.

“Everyone thought this might be his final farewell tour, but he’s actually had a very good season. It’s part of the reason why we’re seeing Jeremy Jacquet playing ever so well. You’ve got [Giovanni] Leoni there as well, the young Italian central defender.

“From what I’m hearing, Andoni Iraola really wants to keep [Van Dijk] around. Captain figure – it’s like having a coach on the pitch. He’s not missing any games; he’s playing really well.

“I’m told there’s every chance he gets another 12 months at least. It doesn’t stop them [from] bringing another centre-half in, but learning from Van Dijk, these youngsters… I’m told Jacquet is learning so much playing next to him.”

That Bailey spoke of how Jacquet is learning plentifully from Van Dijk speaks volumes for the continued importance of the captain to this Liverpool side.

A number of experienced stalwarts have left over the past couple of years, most notably Mo Salah and Andy Robertson at the end of last season, so the ongoing presence of the Dutchman brings a much-needed sense of stability to a team which has undergone significant transition since the start of 2025.

If the 35-year-old agrees a new deal at Anfield, it won’t be a case of sentimentality clouding the club’s judgement – FSG are notoriously reluctant to hand out lucrative contract extensions to players over 30, so for the skipper to even have a plausible chance of getting one says a lot for the influence that he still exerts on the pitch.

Van Dijk is more than experienced enough to not give anything away publicly unless he’s sure that there are major developments behind the scenes about his future, so it doesn’t surprise us that he’s been coy on the subject.

A decision will need to be reached before the season ends, but considering that he didn’t pen his previous extension until two months from his prior deal expiring, there’s still ample time for the defender to agree new terms with Liverpool and continue his hallowed legacy into the 2027/28 campaign at least.

#2005. Osmand proves he's no Honda Civic... and now he's ready to motor on for Celtic

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EST, 7 November 2026

When Brendan Rodgers returns to Glasgow for a Q&A session next June, it would feel like a waste of time for him to be grilled on the exact reasons behind his team selection for matches which, by then, will have taken place almost two years ago.

Frankly, those assembled in the Royal Concert Hall that evening will have their mind on other matters.

Nonetheless, there remains a curiosity about why the Northern Irishman overlooked Callum Osmand at a time when Celtic were evidently crying out for a spark up front.

Rodgers, you may well remember, had spoken with great excitement about the club signing the player from Fulham a few weeks previously.

Sure, Osmand was only 19 at the time. He hadn't played a single minute of first-team football, either.

But as a combination of Daizen Maeda and the soon-to-depart Adam Idah failed to find the net across 210 minutes against Kairat Almaty, you couldn't help but wonder if the much-vaunted teenager stationed on the bench in both legs might have been worth a shot.

Despite Rodgers giving Osmand the big build up that summer, the forward didn't play a single minute prior to his abrupt departure at the end of October.

While that was clearly his prerogative, the impact Osmand has made across an injury-stricken year does suggest that it was an oversight.

Handed his debut as a substitute by Martin O'Neill against Falkirk soon after, Osmand scored a brilliant flashing header in the League Cup semi-final against Rangers before sustaining a serious hamstring tear against Midtjylland.

Only back in contention on the final day of the season after surgery, he set up Maeda and scored himself as Celtic clinched the title in dramatic fashion against Hearts.

Having been sidelined again with an ankle injury at the outset of this campaign, he's rebounded in some style. His goal and assist for Camilo Duran against Besiktas on Thursday came a couple of weeks after scoring twice in a 7-1 rout against the Tynecastle men in what was his first senior start.

Callum Osmand made an instant impression off the bench against Besiktas

After just 13 matches for Celtic, it may be a little too early to describe Osmand as a Ferrari. But a Honda Civic, he is most certainly not.

The beauty of the situation, from the club's perspective, is that the player hasn't even revved the engine as he sets out on his career path.

Osmand, who turns 21 as Kilmarnock visit today, looks first-team ready any time he's taken the field. Yet he's the first to admit that the game-time those injuries denied him stunted his development.

Provided there's a fair wind at his back, though, he's certain there's a lot more to come.

'I would say I'm nowhere near where I want to be personally,' he said.

'There's stuff I need to tidy up on, like decision-making and all this stuff.

'But I feel like the more games I play, the more I understand and the more I learn.

'So, on a personal note, that's what I'd want to do - just keep learning and keep understanding my role within the team and obviously the players you're playing with.

'I've still only played a handful of games, so it's tough learning. But I feel like when you get thrown in the deep end, it's the best way to learn. You learn more off the worst games than the good games.

'It's just as long as I can get better every game, that's all I really want to focus on.'

There's no doubt, though, that there are many moments when he looks the real deal.

For instance, his brilliant finish after Callum McGregor's square ball on Thursday, his first touch after coming off the bench.

'It was crazy,' he smiled. 'It's a surreal feeling when it's my first touch as well.

'I was a bit nervous that I'd shanked it, but no, I'm happy that I caught it nicely.'

One of his next involvements wasn't too bad, either. Motoring into space off the left flank, Osmand had to find the perfect weight and direction on the pass which would allow Camilo Duran to exploit a pocket of space and round the keeper. He could not have played it better.

Osmand has struck up a good understanding with fellow Celtic striker Camilo Duran

'I thought he was offside, to be honest,' he recalled of the moment in which Celtic moved 2-1 in front.

'I was looking at the bench saying 'Close?' and they were like, "Yeah, it's tight".

'But I know where he's going. He's such a sharp striker, so I know if I put that in the space, the keeper is not getting anywhere near it. He's a top, top player, so I can't fault him at all.'

With all due respect to Colby Donovan – also assured after coming off the bench – Thursday night will long be remembered for the belated contributions of Osmand and Duran, who scored three goals between them.

The Colombian began on the right flank, but moved infield once Kasper Hogh tired. The understanding Duran had with Osmand was clear throughout and ultimately proved the undoing of the Turks.

'He's unbelievable, a really top player,' Osmand said. 'You can just see even by the way he walks and the way he moves.

'I learn off him every day. He's an amazing guy. His English is really not great, but somehow we manage to talk to each other a lot.

'I think I find him quite a good friend of mine now.

'And although we might not speak many words, you can tell just by looking ... I don't know how to describe it. Like we talk to each other a lot. Maybe it's little words, but I feel like we get on really well. He's a great guy.'

Duran's finish at the second attempt to seal the victory later on felt hugely significant for all associated with Celtic.

It was precisely the kind of big win at the right moment which O'Neill and his embattled squad needed to blow away the storm clouds. On such moments, entire seasons can hinge and reputations are forged.

'For us, it felt like a must win, like that was our sort of mindset going into that,' Osmand said.

'I think the boys did amazing, so hopefully we just get some confidence and build on from this and that gives us confidence to play more free and take more risks.

'Sometimes when you're not as confident, it's tough to play the football you want to play.'

Manchester City's Phil Foden is struggling to return to the same significant impact he once had at the Etihad.

His influence in the final third has been diminished, with Foden failing to impact multiple games across this campaign.

The 26-year-old has the technical ability to dictate the game, and for a player who was once seemingly undroppable at points under Pep Guardiola, this fall-off is concerning.

Foden now faces a fight to re-establish himself, with his worrying stats from this Premier League season emerging.

His talent and quality will not have disappeared overnight as he continues to struggle under Maresca.

As per FotMob, Foden is clearly a player lacking confidence, with him ranking in the 17.9th percentile for dribble success at 27.3 per cent.

Even just last season, Foden ended the season with 53.2 per cent dribble success.

Maresca is also seemingly not being too impressed, as Foden has only started four of his eight Premier League appearances this season.

In terms of duels, Foden is also losing more than he is winning, with a success rate of 47.9 per cent.

The Englishman does have three goal contributions in the league; however, two of his assists came in the same game as his goal in another.

While the numbers look good on the surface, you would rather those contributions be spread over a number of matches, rather than a select few good displays.

Man City are well stocked in the areas that Foden typically would start in.

Out wide, Iliman Ndiaye and Jeremy Doku seem to be the current first-choice options, while Rayan Cherki has been excellent as the number 10.

Foden's performances have made it difficult to even consider him as an option in any of those positions, and that will be even harder once Antoine Semenyo returns from injury.

This leaves the England international with a tough peak to climb at Man City, with the midfielder needing to prove in his performances that he is the player he once was under Guardiola.

#2001. 'This club's not used to losing' - keeper Johnstone opens up on Celtic struggles

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EST, 7 November 2026

Sam Johnstone has warned that Thursday's dramatic win over Besiktas must be seen as just the first step on Celtic's road to recovery.

The pulsating 3-2 triumph over the Turks came after Martin O'Neill's men had lost four straight matches in Europe with just three wins in the previous ten matches in all competitions.

As timely as the result was, the keeper believes there's a lot of hard work for the side to get through before anyone can talk about it being a turning point in what's been a trying season to this stage.

Asked if the spirit in the camp had been affected by a string of adverse results, Johnstone said: 'Of course it has. I think the results affect it.

'This club's not used to losing and we've probably lost too many games for this club.

'We all realise that, but we have to put things right in each game.

'The lads go out to win every game, so the camp's good.

'It was tough. We're honest players, we're honest people and honest with each other.

'You could see on Thursday night that the lads put a good fight in and got the result.'

Signed on loan from Wolves for the season, Johnstone was handed his chance by O'Neill only to drop out of the team following an indifferent display in the 3-0 loss at Ibrox on September 13.

Celtic goalkeeper is finding his feet in Scottish football after a difficult start

But having been selected ahead of Viljami Sinisalo in the past five matches, the former England goalkeeper believes he's steadily making progress.

'To get a run of games for any player, you find your rhythm,' Johnstone explained.

'It was a new club for me, a new team, so that takes probably a couple of games to get used to as well.

'I think I've got to get used to them (defenders), they've got to get used to me and that only happens through playing and through games. It's great to be in the team.

'It's good. I love playing. It's a great team to play in, a great club to play for and we keep taking it game by game. We go again on Sunday.'

Johnstone moved to Celtic at the start of a difficult period which saw the side struggle for consistency.

Adamant that he's never regretted moving up to Scotland for a minute, however, he added: 'The expectation, rightly so, for this place is to win games.

'Unfortunately, we hadn't quite met that expectation and the lads know that.

'Like I said, we try to win every game and put things right.

Celtic fought back for a much-needed Europa League victory against Besiktas

'It's brilliant to play for this club. The passion of the fans, good and bad. The standard of players on the pitch, day in, day out at training.

'When I came, I said I didn't have to think twice about coming here.'

Having heard so much about Celtic Park on the night of a big European win, the keeper was glad to finally witness it for himself.

'It was unbelievable to experience this place, rocking and get the win,' he reflected.

'It's a great feeling. It's great to play in front of and feel the passion of the fans. That does help the lads and drives the lads on.

'As you could see, there were times in the game where we struggled a little bit, but the lads dug in. It's never going to be easy.

'In the Europa League, you're playing top teams and, after last week's result as well, we were under a lot of pressure. The lads came up with the goods.

'We've still got a chance to qualify, and that's our aim, so we'll take the next game the same as any other game, that we go to win.'

The city of Istanbul has left an indelible mark in Liverpool’s European history from the epic 2005 Champions League final against AC Milan, but recent visits to the Turkish capital have been bruising.

With Galatasaray currently 18th in the league phase standings, it’s not inconceivable that they and Liverpool could meet at some point in the knockout rounds yet again next spring, but we’d imagine that the Reds have had their fill of visits to Istanbul after the past 14 months.

Tel came back on but was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes and Leeds went on to win the game 1-0

His performances earned him a place in the first-team picture, making his senior debut in October 2021 during a 2-1 Championship victory over Barnsley at Ashton Gate.

After leaving Bristol City in the summer of 2025, the midfielder joined Plymouth Argyle, adding further senior experience in League One and domestic cup competitions to his footballing CV.

Deals for Wickham and Benarous are both subject to the usual EFL and FA Approvals.

#1989. ‘If I stayed…’ – Rio Ngumoha reflects on ‘no-brainer’ decision to swap Chelsea for Liverpool

Rio Ngumoha has said that his decision to swap Chelsea for Liverpool in 2024 was a ‘no-brainer’.

The Reds signed the teenage winger from the London club’s academy just after he turned 16, with a subsequent tribunal determining that the Merseysiders were to pay an initial £2.8m (potentially rising to £6.8m) in compensation.

The now 18-year-old has gone on to make 44 appearances and counting for LFC’s first team, along with winning three senior England caps, and he’s turned in some man-of-the-match performances at Champions League level.

In a recent media interview (via The Standard), Ngumoha explained that he decided to leave Chelsea for Liverpool because he saw a clearer pathway to the first team at Anfield than he did in west London.

The winger said: “I needed a new challenge. I feel like if I stayed at Chelsea… not saying I wouldn’t have got to the first team as quickly, because I believe in my ability, but I feel Liverpool just gave me a new pathway.

“The plan they set for me was straightforward. For me, it was a no-brainer going to Liverpool.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The Reds have had a fine track record for attracting top-class teenage talents in recent years, and Ngumoha is perhaps the standout signing in that category.

That Liverpool were prepared to go through a rigorous registration process with the Premier League (as the winger was a minor at the time) shows just how determined they were to see the deal through, and all of that bureaucratic effort has proven to be more than worth it.

In little more than a year, the teenager has gone from highly-rated prospect to established first-team presence, and there’s a palpable excitement among the fans at Anfield every time he gets the ball, with many a defender bamboozled by his phenomenal dribbling ability and supreme self-confidence.

Ngumoha’s leap of faith in joining the Reds has been vindicated by his regularity of senior football, especially this season as he’s started almost half of our matches across all competitions, and full credit to him for seizing his opportunity when it’s been handed to him.

Chelsea’s loss has very much proven to be our gain, and with the 18-year-old now holding a market value of €50m (£41.8m), that aforementioned compensation fee looks increasingly like one of the steals of the century.

Chema Andres has been doing Brighton's dirty work as they have climbed into the Premier League's top four.

New Premier League data is emerging after 10 games, showing just how important he has been.

And that will certainly catch attention across the league.

#1985. Three Bridges show fighting spirit to earn point against Brentwood Town

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Three Bridges produced a spirited performance on Saturday at Jubilee Field, earning a 1-1 draw against Brentwood Town after an evenly contested encounter. Bridges were desperate to get points on the board, but perhaps even more importantly, to rediscover the battling spirit that had been missing during last week's disappointing performance away at Maldon & Tiptree. Jamie Crellin's men responded positively, showing plenty of fight and determination throughout.

After an even opening, the hosts took the lead in the 12th minute through October's Club Player of the Month, Ade Adeyinka. David Przybylo played Ade through the middle and, from around 20 yards out, he unleashed an unstoppable strike into the net to give Bridges an early advantage.

The remainder of the first half was evenly matched, with Roberts producing several good saves in the Bridges goal. At the other end, the energetic Villavicencio continued to cause problems for the visitors, particularly with a dangerous cross towards Reece Hallard, whose header from six yards narrowly missed the target. Bridges went into the interval holding a deserved 1-0 lead.

It could have been 2-0 just moments into the second half as, straight from the restart, Bridges put together an excellent move down the right. Velvick released Przybylo through on goal, but under pressure from the goalkeeper, his effort narrowly drifted wide.

Brentwood Town began to pile on the pressure at the other end and found their reward in the 58th minute. Following a free-kick from Reid, Gibbs slotted his effort into the bottom corner to restore parity.

Just a couple of minutes later, Przybylo, who had been a constant handful for the visitors, worked his way past his marker and had another opportunity to restore Bridges' advantage, but his effort narrowly missed the far post.

With Bridges short of options on the bench and several players playing through injuries, maintaining the intensity became increasingly difficult. Brentwood Town took control during the final 20 minutes, but Roberts came to the rescue with two superb saves to deny Cerulli and Sears, while the Bridges players continued to put their bodies on the line to protect their point.

There was late drama in the 94th minute when Reece Hallard chased a ball through on the counter-attack, only for Cripps to handle it as the last man. The Brentwood defender was shown a straight red card, leaving the visitors down to ten men. However, it came too late to have any impact on the outcome, as the match finished 1-1.

The point represents a much-needed response from Bridges, who will now face a demanding run of three consecutive away fixtures in seven days. First up is a trip to Cray Wanderers on Tuesday 10 November (19:45), followed by a visit to Welling United on Saturday 14 November (15:00), before another Tuesday evening journey to Dartford on 17 November (19:45).

Three Bridges Line-up: Roberts, Irving, Neathey (C), Malone, J. Hallard, Villavicencio (Chambers 87), Adeyinka, Przybylo (Richards 77), Velvick, R. Hallard, Bennett.

Player of the Match – Sam Roberts: An impressive display from Roberts in goal, producing several outstanding saves to keep Bridges in the contest. The young goalkeeper also impressed with his distribution, setting his side on the attack with some excellent kicking. A thoroughly deserved Player of the Match award.

#1983. Oliver Glasner has plan to replicate 'unpleasant' Crystal Palace move at Nottingham Forest - expert

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner will attempt to turn the City Ground into a fortress in a similar way to what he did when he was at Crystal Palace.

That is the opinion of experienced former Tottenham, Everton and Aston Villa scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

Selhurst Park became a difficult place to visit when the Austrian was in charge, with the Eagles attempting to create an intimidating atmosphere for their opponents.

Before Saturday, Glasner had failed to oversee even a single goal scored at the City Ground this season, with the pressure mounting on him at Nottingham Forest.

But his team looked transformed as they beat Manchester City 3-1, taking full advantage of the hostile atmosphere to crush Enzo Maresca's team from the first whistle.

Nottingham Forest and Glasner will hope to keep the momentum building after the international break, with Chelsea the next team set to visit the City Ground.

Telling contributions at both ends from Jair. 😤🇧🇷 pic.twitter.com/Msbcwp0NfM

It was clear from the first whistle that Nottingham Forest were determined to get into Man City's faces.

Centre-back Jair Cunha went as far as to press Josko Gvardiol mid-way into the Man City half, winning the ball back and opening the score when he finished well past Gianluigi Donnarumma.

"The way the game started, you had to worry. The first 15 minutes, they were flying, Nottingham Forest," King told Football Insider.

"They were putting in tackles, and they were hurting people. Closing down quick. Forest looked a bit like Crystal Palace when they played at home under Glasner.

"Selhurst Park was an unpleasant place to go to for teams, and the City Ground could certainly be the same, if he gets them going like they did on Saturday."

On paper, the City Ground should be one of the most difficult places to travel to in the Premier League.

Nottingham Forest's ground is almost always loud and very enclosed, with little space in between the pitch and the fans.

Under Nuno Espirito Santo it lived up to that tag, with his team losing just five of 19 games played there in the 2024-25 Premier League season.

Last season, the City Ground saw just four Premier League wins at home - that number must be addressed by Glasner, and Saturday's game was a good start.

#1980. ‘Unlikely to be…’ – Journalist sounds contract renewal warning over Van Dijk and Alisson

Liverpool fans have been advised that prospective contract renewals for Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker could take time to materialise.

The future of both long-serving players has been in the spotlight this week after they publicly addressed their respective situations, with the goalkeeper’s agent already in talks with club chiefs while the captain has maintained a more neutral ‘let’s see’ stance.

Their current deals are set to expire next June, and they’ll be able to sign pre-contract agreements with overseas clubs from the beginning of January unless they extend their terms with the Reds before then.

In an article for The Athletic discussing the futures of Van Dijk and Alisson, James Pearce warned that ‘there is unlikely to be a quick resolution’ to either player’s contract situation, citing how renewals for the Dutchman and Mo Salah two seasons ago weren’t confirmed until April 2025.

The journalist explained how Liverpool would need to take a pragmatic approach to the renewal process and not be led by sentiment, with the defender turning 36 next July and the goalkeeper’s 35th birthday coming three months later.

In a more hopeful note, Pearce wrote: ‘It makes sense for all parties to wait and see how things unfold in the coming weeks and months. Respect abounds and relationships are strong, with dialogue ongoing between sporting director Julian Ward and the pair’s camps.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The case studies of Van Dijk and Salah from 2024/25 indicate that we ought not to expect a swift resolution to the current contract situations regarding the Dutchman and Alisson, with negotiations set to involve substantial back-and-forth before any agreement is struck.

Considering ther importance on the pitch, they’re two of the highest-earning players in the current Liverpool squad, with the captain leading the way on £350,000 per week and the goalkeeper pocketing a weekly wage of £250,000 (Capology).

For their deals to be renewed, it’d either take a significant deflection from club policy to hand out lucrative extensions to players in their mid-30s, or the pair to accept a reduction on their base salary and increase the value of performance-related bonuses on offer.

In truth, the contract negotiations for Van Dijk and Alisson will likely run for another few months, and there could be some frayed nerves among Kopites if either or both situations were still unresolved by spring.

However, with the duo proving this season that they remain top-class performers bringing some crucial stability to a much-changed team, Ward must make every effort to keep them at Anfield for at least another year, and we’re cautiously optimistic that both will remain Reds players going into the 2027/28 campaign.
